questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Counters P and Q sold 112 tickets together. How many did P sell? I. P sold 2 more than Q. II. P sold more than 40 tickets.
questions.explanation: The total and exact difference determine P. A lower bound alone leaves several possible counts.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A service by Anantapur has a total of 260 seats in two coaches. How many seats does coach A have? I. A has more seats than B. II. B has exactly 105 seats.
questions.explanation: Subtract the known B count from the total. Knowing only which is larger does not determine the count.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A dispatcher at Anantapur sees two queues. Is the service rate of X higher than that of Y? I. X serves three times as many people. II. X takes twice as long for that number. Both counts are positive.
questions.explanation: The rate comparison needs both the count ratio and the time ratio. Together they give X at 1.5 times Y.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three docks dispatched 31, 41, and 51 parcels in some order. B dispatched more than C. A did not dispatch the fewest or the most. What was B’s count?
questions.explanation: A must be the middle dock. Of the remaining two, B is larger.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three weekly totals average 81. The first two were 66 and 91. What was the final total?
questions.explanation: Multiply the mean by three, then subtract the two known observations.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An office in Anantapur moves a help desk next to the numbered gates to cut requests for directions. Which assumption is needed?
options: All visitors prefer speaking to an official.
The desk handles refunds at every gate.
The number of gates will decrease.
Some people needing directions can find the relocated desk.
questions.explanation: For the relocation to affect direction requests, at least some intended users must be able to reach the desk.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: After a digital guide was installed at Anantapur, missed connections fell. Which observation most weakens the argument that the guide caused the reduction?
options: The guide uses larger text than the old notice.
The total number of express routes remained steady.
Users consulted the guide on both weekdays and weekends.
The timetable simultaneously lengthened the connection windows.
questions.explanation: More time to connect is an alternative explanation that changed when the guide changed.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Anantapur, two switches start open. An indicator turns on exactly when one switch is closed. The first switch is now closed and the indicator is off. What follows?
questions.explanation: With the first switch closed, an open second switch would turn the indicator on.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: The rule at Anantapur states that each accepted request has a reference number. Request 31 has no reference number. What can be concluded?
options: The request was accepted with a special code.
All requests without account IDs are accepted.
questions.explanation: An accepted request necessarily has a reference number. Its absence rules out acceptance.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 3:06?
questions.explanation: The minute hand is at 36°. The hour hand is at 93°. Take the smaller angular separation.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A review at Anantapur was held on Tuesday. What weekday is the next review if it is 52 days later?
questions.explanation: The day shift is the remainder when 52 is divided by seven.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Asha is the sister of Deepa. Deepa is the mother of Hema. How is Asha related to Hema?
questions.explanation: The person described is the sister of the child’s mother.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What negates the claim “Every consignment checked at Anantapur was both tagged and sealed”?
options: Every checked consignment was untagged and unsealed.
Some checked consignments were both tagged and sealed.
At least one checked consignment was untagged or unsealed.
questions.explanation: To refute the universal claim, one checked consignment need only fail either requirement.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Anantapur, exactly two tasks are selected from A, B, C and D. Choosing A requires C. Tasks B and C cannot both be selected. Which pair is valid?
questions.explanation: The pair includes A’s prerequisite and avoids the prohibited combination.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Some enquiries at Anantapur are forwarded. Every forwarded enquiry receives a tracking number. Some enquiries are urgent. What is certain?
options: Every enquiry with a tracking number is urgent.
No enquiry with a tracking number is urgent.
questions.explanation: At least one forwarded enquiry exists, and every forwarded enquiry receives a number. Urgency is unrelated in the premises.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Only one of Asha, Deepa and Hema signed a receipt. Asha says that Deepa signed it. Deepa says that Hema signed it. Hema says that Deepa did not sign it. Exactly two statements are true. Who signed it?
questions.explanation: The statements by the first and third people are complements. The middle statement must be true as well.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A box may leave shelf 41 only when it has passed inspection and has a collection code. A box has passed inspection and lacks a collection code. What follows?
options: It may not leave under this rule.
It necessarily belongs to another shelf.
questions.explanation: Passing inspection meets one requirement. A collection code is also required.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Surveyors at Anantapur interviewed only passengers who arrived before 08:00. Most interviewed passengers favoured a morning service. Which conclusion is defensible?
options: Most passengers at all hours favoured the service.
The survey sampled all types of passengers equally.
Most members of the interviewed group favoured the service.
questions.explanation: The survey supports a statement about its sample. The time restriction limits broader inference.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Anantapur, a form is accepted whenever its two signatures are present. A particular form was not accepted. What must follow?
options: At least one signature was absent.
The form was accepted without a signature.
questions.explanation: If both signatures were present, the rule would guarantee acceptance. Nonacceptance rules out both being present.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: During review 11, case P is earlier than Q. R is earlier than P and S is later than Q. Which case is third in time order?
questions.explanation: The constraints force R, P, Q, S in that order.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Anantapur, all inspected consignments are tagged. No tagged consignment is in bay Z. Some priority consignments are inspected. Which conclusion is forced?
options: Some inspected consignments are in bay Z.
Some priority consignments are outside bay Z.
Every consignment outside bay Z is tagged.
questions.explanation: An inspected priority consignment is tagged and therefore outside bay Z.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Why compare visits per open hour?
options: The sites recorded every visitor’s name.
Opening more hours automatically reduces attendance.
The sites were available for different amounts of time.
Bus schedules were identical at both sites.
questions.explanation: Raw total visits depend partly on how many hours a site was open.
questions.passage: A neighbourhood cooling centre opened on afternoons when the temperature was expected to rise sharply. A second site stayed open on ordinary days as well. The organisers wanted to compare how often each site was used, but the sites were served by different bus routes. They planned to compare visits per open hour and ask where users lived before increasing either site’s hours.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Why do the bus routes matter for the comparison?
options: Access may differ independently of opening hours.
Bus services establish which building is cooler.
Users always reach both centres by bus.
Different bus routes make attendance impossible to record.
questions.explanation: Transport is a plausible difference unrelated to the proposed opening-hour policy.
questions.passage: A neighbourhood cooling centre opened on afternoons when the temperature was expected to rise sharply. A second site stayed open on ordinary days as well. The organisers wanted to compare how often each site was used, but the sites were served by different bus routes. They planned to compare visits per open hour and ask where users lived before increasing either site’s hours.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which finding would most directly support extending hours at one site?
options: Many users who live nearby report arriving after it has closed.
The other site has a brighter sign.
Both sites bought the same fans.
Users who visited early generally arrived on foot.
questions.explanation: People arriving after closure indicate unmet demand during the hours being considered.
questions.passage: A neighbourhood cooling centre opened on afternoons when the temperature was expected to rise sharply. A second site stayed open on ordinary days as well. The organisers wanted to compare how often each site was used, but the sites were served by different bus routes. They planned to compare visits per open hour and ask where users lived before increasing either site’s hours.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which conclusion about the cooling centres goes beyond the passage?
options: One site opens on ordinary days as well.
The same schedule will work equally well in every neighbourhood.
The organisers want an attendance measure that accounts for opening time.
The organisers plan to ask where users live.
questions.explanation: The passage describes two sites and a plan to compare them. It gives no basis for a universal schedule.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete 3, 41, 7, 38, 11, 35, …
questions.explanation: Odd positions increase by four, while even positions decrease by three. The next position is odd.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: What pair follows QE, PF, NH, KK, …? The alphabet wraps around.
questions.explanation: The first letter moves backwards and the second forwards by 1, 2, 3 and then 4 places.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: How is ANANT coded if letters in odd positions advance one place and letters in even positions move back two places, wrapping when necessary?
questions.explanation: Apply the alternating shifts independently to each letter. The transformed letters are B, L, B, L, U.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Encode ANANT by moving every letter back one place and then reversing the result. The letter before A is Z.
questions.explanation: First substitute the preceding letter for each character, then read the substituted word backwards.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person is 11th from the front of a 38-person queue. What is their rank from the back, counting the person?
questions.explanation: Subtract the front rank from the total and add one.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A runner was 9th from the end. After 4 entrants finish behind the runner and two ahead, what is their new rank from the end?
questions.explanation: Only finishers behind the runner increase their rank from the end.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The pair 6 : 48 follows a rule: square the first number and add twice the first number. What pairs with 8?
questions.explanation: Apply n²+2n to 8.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A two-digit number is coded as three times its tens digit plus twice its units digit. What is the code for 25?
questions.explanation: Read the tens and units digits separately and apply the two stated weights.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: There are 6 assignments. Two designated assignments must be consecutive, in either order. If just their leftmost starting slot and their internal order are counted, how many placements are possible?
questions.explanation: The consecutive pair can start in any slot except the last and has two orientations.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person walks 6 m west, then 2 m east and 3 m north. What is the distance from the start?
questions.explanation: The net legs are 4k west and 3k north, so the straight-line distance is the 5k hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In file batch 51, A sits left of B; D immediately follows B; C is first and E is last. What is third in the order?
questions.explanation: After fixing the ends, the three middle positions can only be A, B, D.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In team Anantapur, P scored higher than Q and R. Q scored higher than S but lower than R. Who placed second?
questions.explanation: The four place in descending order P, R, Q, S.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Fill the blank in 4, 9, …, 19, 24.
questions.explanation: The arithmetic progression increases by five.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Apply the same rule as the sequence 1, 2, 6, 12, 36 to find the next term.
questions.explanation: The multipliers alternate between 2 and 3. After ×3 comes ×2.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The quantities 5 and 15 are paired. Applying the same ratio to 10 gives what paired number?
questions.explanation: The second quantity in the example is three times the first.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: At Anantapur, five counters line up in a fixed list. Counter A must come first and counter E last. How many possible orders of the remaining counters meet the requirement that B is before C?
questions.explanation: Of the 3! orders of the middle counters, exactly half have B before C.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Which of these proposed pairs for block 1 fails the rule that the second letter is two alphabet positions after the first, with wraparound?
questions.explanation: The failing pair moves by three positions. The other three move by two.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A number has 1 as its tens digit and 2 as its units digit. What is the difference between the reversed number and the original?
questions.explanation: Swapping digits changes the number by nine times their difference, which is 1.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 4, 7, 13, 22, 34, …
questions.explanation: Differences are successive multiples of 3. The next difference is 15.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 4, 12, 10, 30, 28, …
questions.explanation: Apply ×3 and −2 alternately. The next operation is ×3.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A waiting hall has 12 rows. The first row has 13 seats and each subsequent row has 3 more. How many seats are in the last four rows together?
questions.explanation: The last four rows have L, L−3, L−6 and L−9 seats, where L is the final row count.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A status display refreshes every 8 min and a timer every 12 min. Both refresh at 08:00. How many minutes after 08:00 do they refresh together for the third time, excluding 08:00?
questions.explanation: The joint period is LCM(4k,6k) = 12k, with k = 2. The third joint refresh is after three such periods.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: There are 6 red and 9 blue tokens. Two are sampled without replacement. What is the probability of sampling two reds, to three decimals?
questions.explanation: Multiply the probability of a red first by the conditional probability of another red after one has been removed.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The water level in a cuboid tank of base 10 cm by 24 cm rises from 7 cm to 12 cm when an object is fully submerged. What is the object’s volume?
questions.explanation: The object displaces the base area multiplied by the rise in water level.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A circular island of radius 6 m is surrounded by a walkway 3 m wide. What is the walkway area, in multiples of π?
questions.explanation: Subtract the inner disk from the outer disk: (r+3)²−r² = 6r+9.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 6 m vertical pole casts a 8 m shadow. From the shadow tip what is the cosine of the angle of elevation?
questions.explanation: The right triangle is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle. Cosine is the horizontal side over the hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A metal sheet measures 14 cm by 25 cm and is 4 mm thick. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Convert the thickness to 0.4 cm. Multiplying it by the base area gives 10 times the first side length.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 24 cm³ sample of density 3 g/cm³ is combined with a 16 cm³ sample of density 5 g/cm³ without volume change. What is their combined density?
questions.explanation: The mass is 36k+40k = 76k g and the volume is 20k cm³, where k = 2. Divide to obtain the density.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A component has a mass of 7 kg. What is the decrease in weight when moved from a location with g = 10 m/s² to one with g = 8 m/s²?
questions.explanation: Mass stays constant. Weight changes by the mass times the 2 m/s² difference in g.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 7 kg trolley is pulled east by 49 N and west by 28 N. It starts at rest. How far does it travel in 4 s if the forces are constant?
questions.explanation: The net force is 3 times the mass, giving 3 m/s² east. From rest, distance = ½×3×4².

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A sliding crate is pulled with a horizontal force of 60 N along 6 m. Kinetic friction is 20 N. What is the net work on the crate?
questions.explanation: Only horizontal forces do work here. Their net value is twice the friction force in the direction of travel.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 7 kg object slows from 8 m/s to 4 m/s. Find the magnitude of net work done during braking.
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the kinetic energy decrease is ½m(8²−4²) = 24m.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A lift raises a 35 kg load by 3 m in 6 s at a steady speed. Take g = 10 m/s² and efficiency 75%. What input power is needed to the nearest watt?
questions.explanation: Useful power is (5m)×10×3/6 = 125m watts. Divide by 0.75 to find the input power.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 165 N load acts 20 cm to the left of a frictionless pivot. A 33 N load counterbalances it on the right. What is the right-hand lever arm?
questions.explanation: For equilibrium the moments are equal. The smaller force must have 5 times the lever arm.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Resistors of 4 Ω and 8 Ω are connected in series to 24 V. What power is delivered to the larger resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance is 12 Ω. The series current is 2 A, so the larger resistor receives I²R = 4×8.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two 8 Ω resistors are connected in parallel to 24 V. One branch opens. How much does the current drawn from the source decrease?
questions.explanation: Each connected branch draws V/R = 3 A. Disconnecting one branch removes its 3 A contribution.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 1.5 kW appliance runs for 48 min each day for 10 days. What is its electricity cost at ₹6.50/kWh?
questions.explanation: Forty-eight minutes is 0.8 hour. Multiply power by 8 hours total and then by ₹6.50/kWh.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Mix 200 g of water at 75°C with 600 g at 15°C in an insulated vessel of negligible heat capacity. What is the equilibrium temperature?
questions.explanation: The cooler water has triple the mass. The weighted mean is (75+3×15)/4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A heater transfers 1800 J of energy into a 0.2 kg metal block. If the temperature rises by 15°C, find the block’s specific heat capacity.
questions.explanation: Use c=Q/(mΔT), which gives 1800 divided by 0.2×15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A linear sensor reads 2 units at 0°C and 104 units at 100°C. What is the reading at 40°C, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: Add 40% of the change from zero to boiling to the sensor’s reading at 0°C.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An ideal pulley system has four rope segments supporting a 120 N load. What is the work done at the free end to raise the load 1.5 m?
questions.explanation: In an ideal machine the input work equals the increase in potential energy: weight × height.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The ordered measurements are 2, 5, 8, 10, 12, 17, 22. The smallest is corrected to 27. What is the new median?
questions.explanation: The corrected value moves to the end. The old fifth observation becomes the new fourth observation.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A workshop pays a fixed fee of ₹87 plus ₹7 per unit. It pays ₹325 total. What would the bill have been if it had used 6 fewer units?
questions.explanation: The fee is unchanged. Subtract 6×₹7 from the original bill.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two adjacent interior angles of a parallelogram differ by 4°. What is the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles sum to 180°. The larger is 90° plus half their stated difference.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A depot marks a spare part at ₹1300. It applies discounts of 20% and then 15%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: Multiply the marked price by 0.8×0.85 = 0.68. The second discount applies to the reduced price.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: After selling 30% of its ticket stock, a depot has 140 tickets. How many would remain if it then sold one-seventh of the remaining tickets?
questions.explanation: The second sale leaves six-sevenths of 140. The original stock is unnecessary for this step.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The mean mass of 14 sacks is 41 kg. Four other sacks averaging 45 kg are added. What is the combined mean to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: Add the two total masses before dividing by the new number of sacks.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: P can complete a task in 12 days and Q in 24 days. They work together for 2 days. How many more days does Q need alone?
questions.explanation: Together they complete k(1/(6k)+1/(12k)) = one-quarter. Q completes the remaining three-quarters in 9k days. Here k = 2.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 120 m train travels at 72 km/h and passes a second train moving towards it at 36 km/h. If the entire pass takes 5 seconds, how long is the second train?
questions.explanation: The combined speed is 30 m/s. Multiply by the passing time to get both lengths together and subtract the length of the first train.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A total of 54 tickets cost ₹1680. Regular tickets cost ₹40 and concession tickets cost ₹25. How many regular tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Subtract what all concession tickets would cost from the actual total, then divide the difference by ₹15.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Counters P and Q sold 124 tickets together. How many did P sell? I. P sold 4 more than Q. II. P sold more than 40 tickets.
questions.explanation: The total and exact difference determine P. A lower bound alone leaves several possible counts.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A service by Bapatla has a total of 280 seats in two coaches. How many seats does coach A have? I. A has more seats than B. II. B has exactly 110 seats.
questions.explanation: Subtract the known B count from the total. Knowing only which is larger does not determine the count.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A dispatcher at Bapatla sees two queues. Is the service rate of X higher than that of Y? I. X serves three times as many people. II. X takes twice as long for that number. Both counts are positive.
questions.explanation: The rate comparison needs both the count ratio and the time ratio. Together they give X at 1.5 times Y.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three docks dispatched 32, 42, and 52 parcels in some order. B dispatched more than C. A did not dispatch the fewest or the most. What was B’s count?
questions.explanation: A must be the middle dock. Of the remaining two, B is larger.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three weekly totals average 82. The first two were 67 and 92. What was the final total?
questions.explanation: Multiply the mean by three, then subtract the two known observations.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: After a digital guide was installed at Bapatla, missed connections fell. Which observation most weakens the argument that the guide caused the reduction?
options: The guide uses larger text than the old notice.
The timetable simultaneously lengthened the connection windows.
The total number of express routes remained steady.
Users consulted the guide on both weekdays and weekends.
questions.explanation: More time to connect is an alternative explanation that changed when the guide changed.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Bapatla, two switches start open. An indicator turns on exactly when one switch is closed. The first switch is now closed and the indicator is off. What follows?
questions.explanation: With the first switch closed, an open second switch would turn the indicator on.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: The rule at Bapatla states that each accepted request has a reference number. Request 32 has no reference number. What can be concluded?
options: The request was accepted with a special code.
All requests without account IDs are accepted.
questions.explanation: An accepted request necessarily has a reference number. Its absence rules out acceptance.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 4:07?
questions.explanation: The minute hand is at 42°. The hour hand is at 123.5°. Take the smaller angular separation.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A review at Bapatla was held on Wednesday. What weekday is the next review if it is 56 days later?
questions.explanation: The day shift is the remainder when 56 is divided by seven.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Bina is the sister of Esha. Esha is the mother of Indu. How is Bina related to Indu?
questions.explanation: The person described is the sister of the child’s mother.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What negates the claim “Every consignment checked at Bapatla was both tagged and sealed”?
options: At least one checked consignment was untagged or unsealed.
Every checked consignment was untagged and unsealed.
Some checked consignments were both tagged and sealed.
questions.explanation: To refute the universal claim, one checked consignment need only fail either requirement.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Bapatla, exactly two tasks are selected from A, B, C and D. Choosing A requires C. Tasks B and C cannot both be selected. Which pair is valid?
questions.explanation: The pair includes A’s prerequisite and avoids the prohibited combination.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Some enquiries at Bapatla are forwarded. Every forwarded enquiry receives a tracking number. Some enquiries are urgent. What is certain?
options: Every enquiry with a tracking number is urgent.
No enquiry with a tracking number is urgent.
questions.explanation: At least one forwarded enquiry exists, and every forwarded enquiry receives a number. Urgency is unrelated in the premises.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Only one of Bina, Esha and Indu signed a receipt. Bina says that Esha signed it. Esha says that Indu signed it. Indu says that Esha did not sign it. Exactly two statements are true. Who signed it?
questions.explanation: The statements by the first and third people are complements. The middle statement must be true as well.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A box may leave shelf 42 only when it has passed inspection and has a collection code. A box has passed inspection and lacks a collection code. What follows?
options: It may not leave under this rule.
It necessarily belongs to another shelf.
questions.explanation: Passing inspection meets one requirement. A collection code is also required.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Surveyors at Bapatla interviewed only passengers who arrived before 08:00. Most interviewed passengers favoured a morning service. Which conclusion is defensible?
options: Most passengers at all hours favoured the service.
Most members of the interviewed group favoured the service.
The survey sampled all types of passengers equally.
questions.explanation: The survey supports a statement about its sample. The time restriction limits broader inference.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Bapatla, a form is accepted whenever its two signatures are present. A particular form was not accepted. What must follow?
options: At least one signature was absent.
The form was accepted without a signature.
questions.explanation: If both signatures were present, the rule would guarantee acceptance. Nonacceptance rules out both being present.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: During review 12, case P is earlier than Q. R is earlier than P and S is later than Q. Which case is third in time order?
questions.explanation: The constraints force R, P, Q, S in that order.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Bapatla, all inspected consignments are tagged. No tagged consignment is in bay Z. Some priority consignments are inspected. Which conclusion is forced?
options: Some priority consignments are outside bay Z.
Some inspected consignments are in bay Z.
Every consignment outside bay Z is tagged.
questions.explanation: An inspected priority consignment is tagged and therefore outside bay Z.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An office in Bapatla moves a help desk next to the numbered gates to cut requests for directions. Which assumption is needed?
options: All visitors prefer speaking to an official.
Some people needing directions can find the relocated desk.
The desk handles refunds at every gate.
The number of gates will decrease.
questions.explanation: For the relocation to affect direction requests, at least some intended users must be able to reach the desk.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What is the chief purpose of tracking titles in both formats?
options: To separate the influence of format from the appeal of a particular title.
To replace the printed collection with a listening room.
To record which devices residents own.
To estimate the cost of printing each title.
questions.explanation: Holding the story constant makes differences between the audio and print forms easier to compare.
questions.passage: A library offered audiobooks to residents who could not comfortably read its small-print fiction. Borrowing rose, although several new titles arrived that month. When the team surveyed borrowers, some praised the larger collection and others said they could listen while travelling. The library plans to track titles offered in both formats and compare changes in borrowing for the same title.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Why does the arrival of new titles complicate interpretation?
options: The titles prevented users from listening on journeys.
The selection was held identical across the two periods.
The survey counted purchases instead of loans.
The changing selection could itself increase borrowing.
questions.explanation: A new title can draw borrowers regardless of the format in which it is offered.
questions.passage: A library offered audiobooks to residents who could not comfortably read its small-print fiction. Borrowing rose, although several new titles arrived that month. When the team surveyed borrowers, some praised the larger collection and others said they could listen while travelling. The library plans to track titles offered in both formats and compare changes in borrowing for the same title.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which mechanism for audiobook use is supported by borrower comments?
options: All readers switch because travelling becomes cheaper.
Libraries can stop buying printed titles.
Most users read only at home.
questions.explanation: Travelling listeners are explicitly among the reasons respondents gave.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What tone does the passage take toward the borrowing increase?
options: Encouraging yet open to competing explanations.
Certain that the format is the sole cause.
Primarily concerned with enforcing borrowing limits.
questions.explanation: It reports benefits alongside an alternative explanation and proposes further comparison.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: How is BAPAT coded if letters in odd positions advance one place and letters in even positions move back two places, wrapping when necessary?
questions.explanation: Apply the alternating shifts independently to each letter. The transformed letters are C, Y, Q, Y, U.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Encode BAPAT by moving every letter back one place and then reversing the result. The letter before A is Z.
questions.explanation: First substitute the preceding letter for each character, then read the substituted word backwards.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person is 12th from the front of a 40-person queue. What is their rank from the back, counting the person?
questions.explanation: Subtract the front rank from the total and add one.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A runner was 10th from the end. After 5 entrants finish behind the runner and two ahead, what is their new rank from the end?
questions.explanation: Only finishers behind the runner increase their rank from the end.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The pair 7 : 63 follows a rule: square the first number and add twice the first number. What pairs with 9?
questions.explanation: Apply n²+2n to 9.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A two-digit number is coded as three times its tens digit plus twice its units digit. What is the code for 26?
questions.explanation: Read the tens and units digits separately and apply the two stated weights.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: There are 7 assignments. Two designated assignments must be consecutive, in either order. If just their leftmost starting slot and their internal order are counted, how many placements are possible?
questions.explanation: The consecutive pair can start in any slot except the last and has two orientations.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person walks 12 m west, then 4 m east and 6 m north. What is the distance from the start?
questions.explanation: The net legs are 4k west and 3k north, so the straight-line distance is the 5k hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In file batch 52, A sits left of B; D immediately follows B; C is first and E is last. What is third in the order?
questions.explanation: After fixing the ends, the three middle positions can only be A, B, D.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In team Bapatla, P scored higher than Q and R. Q scored higher than S but lower than R. Who placed second?
questions.explanation: The four place in descending order P, R, Q, S.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Fill the blank in 5, 10, …, 20, 25.
questions.explanation: The arithmetic progression increases by five.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Apply the same rule as the sequence 2, 4, 12, 24, 72 to find the next term.
questions.explanation: The multipliers alternate between 2 and 3. After ×3 comes ×2.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The quantities 6 and 18 are paired. Applying the same ratio to 11 gives what paired number?
questions.explanation: The second quantity in the example is three times the first.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: At Bapatla, five counters line up in a fixed list. Counter A must come first and counter E last. How many possible orders of the remaining counters meet the requirement that B is before C?
questions.explanation: Of the 3! orders of the middle counters, exactly half have B before C.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Which of these proposed pairs for block 2 fails the rule that the second letter is two alphabet positions after the first, with wraparound?
questions.explanation: The failing pair moves by three positions. The other three move by two.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A number has 1 as its tens digit and 3 as its units digit. What is the difference between the reversed number and the original?
questions.explanation: Swapping digits changes the number by nine times their difference, which is 2.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 5, 9, 17, 29, 45, …
questions.explanation: Differences are successive multiples of 4. The next difference is 20.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 5, 15, 13, 39, 37, …
questions.explanation: Apply ×3 and −2 alternately. The next operation is ×3.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete 4, 42, 8, 39, 12, 36, …
questions.explanation: Odd positions increase by four, while even positions decrease by three. The next position is odd.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: What pair follows RF, QG, OI, LL, …? The alphabet wraps around.
questions.explanation: The first letter moves backwards and the second forwards by 1, 2, 3 and then 4 places.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The water level in a cuboid tank of base 15 cm by 24 cm rises from 7 cm to 13 cm when an object is fully submerged. What is the object’s volume?
questions.explanation: The object displaces the base area multiplied by the rise in water level.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A circular island of radius 7 m is surrounded by a walkway 3 m wide. What is the walkway area, in multiples of π?
questions.explanation: Subtract the inner disk from the outer disk: (r+3)²−r² = 6r+9.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 9 m vertical pole casts a 12 m shadow. From the shadow tip what is the cosine of the angle of elevation?
questions.explanation: The right triangle is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle. Cosine is the horizontal side over the hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A metal sheet measures 15 cm by 25 cm and is 4 mm thick. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Convert the thickness to 0.4 cm. Multiplying it by the base area gives 10 times the first side length.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 36 cm³ sample of density 3 g/cm³ is combined with a 24 cm³ sample of density 5 g/cm³ without volume change. What is their combined density?
questions.explanation: The mass is 36k+40k = 76k g and the volume is 20k cm³, where k = 3. Divide to obtain the density.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A component has a mass of 8 kg. What is the decrease in weight when moved from a location with g = 10 m/s² to one with g = 8 m/s²?
questions.explanation: Mass stays constant. Weight changes by the mass times the 2 m/s² difference in g.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 8 kg trolley is pulled east by 56 N and west by 32 N. It starts at rest. How far does it travel in 4 s if the forces are constant?
questions.explanation: The net force is 3 times the mass, giving 3 m/s² east. From rest, distance = ½×3×4².

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A sliding crate is pulled with a horizontal force of 75 N along 7 m. Kinetic friction is 25 N. What is the net work on the crate?
questions.explanation: Only horizontal forces do work here. Their net value is twice the friction force in the direction of travel.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 8 kg object slows from 8 m/s to 4 m/s. Find the magnitude of net work done during braking.
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the kinetic energy decrease is ½m(8²−4²) = 24m.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A lift raises a 40 kg load by 3 m in 6 s at a steady speed. Take g = 10 m/s² and efficiency 75%. What input power is needed to the nearest watt?
questions.explanation: Useful power is (5m)×10×3/6 = 125m watts. Divide by 0.75 to find the input power.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 204 N load acts 20 cm to the left of a frictionless pivot. A 34 N load counterbalances it on the right. What is the right-hand lever arm?
questions.explanation: For equilibrium the moments are equal. The smaller force must have 6 times the lever arm.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Resistors of 5 Ω and 10 Ω are connected in series to 30 V. What power is delivered to the larger resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance is 15 Ω. The series current is 2 A, so the larger resistor receives I²R = 4×10.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two 10 Ω resistors are connected in parallel to 30 V. One branch opens. How much does the current drawn from the source decrease?
questions.explanation: Each connected branch draws V/R = 3 A. Disconnecting one branch removes its 3 A contribution.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 1.75 kW appliance runs for 48 min each day for 10 days. What is its electricity cost at ₹6.50/kWh?
questions.explanation: Forty-eight minutes is 0.8 hour. Multiply power by 8 hours total and then by ₹6.50/kWh.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Mix 300 g of water at 75°C with 900 g at 15°C in an insulated vessel of negligible heat capacity. What is the equilibrium temperature?
questions.explanation: The cooler water has triple the mass. The weighted mean is (75+3×15)/4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A heater transfers 2700 J of energy into a 0.3 kg metal block. If the temperature rises by 15°C, find the block’s specific heat capacity.
questions.explanation: Use c=Q/(mΔT), which gives 2700 divided by 0.3×15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A linear sensor reads 3 units at 0°C and 106 units at 100°C. What is the reading at 40°C, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: Add 40% of the change from zero to boiling to the sensor’s reading at 0°C.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An ideal pulley system has four rope segments supporting a 180 N load. What is the work done at the free end to raise the load 1.5 m?
questions.explanation: In an ideal machine the input work equals the increase in potential energy: weight × height.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The ordered measurements are 3, 6, 9, 11, 13, 18, 23. The smallest is corrected to 28. What is the new median?
questions.explanation: The corrected value moves to the end. The old fifth observation becomes the new fourth observation.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A workshop pays a fixed fee of ₹88 plus ₹7 per unit. It pays ₹340 total. What would the bill have been if it had used 6 fewer units?
questions.explanation: The fee is unchanged. Subtract 6×₹7 from the original bill.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two adjacent interior angles of a parallelogram differ by 6°. What is the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles sum to 180°. The larger is 90° plus half their stated difference.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A depot marks a spare part at ₹1400. It applies discounts of 20% and then 15%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: Multiply the marked price by 0.8×0.85 = 0.68. The second discount applies to the reduced price.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: After selling 30% of its ticket stock, a depot has 147 tickets. How many would remain if it then sold one-seventh of the remaining tickets?
questions.explanation: The second sale leaves six-sevenths of 147. The original stock is unnecessary for this step.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The mean mass of 16 sacks is 41 kg. Four other sacks averaging 46 kg are added. What is the combined mean to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: Add the two total masses before dividing by the new number of sacks.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: P can complete a task in 18 days and Q in 36 days. They work together for 3 days. How many more days does Q need alone?
questions.explanation: Together they complete k(1/(6k)+1/(12k)) = one-quarter. Q completes the remaining three-quarters in 9k days. Here k = 3.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 144 m train travels at 72 km/h and passes a second train moving towards it at 36 km/h. If the entire pass takes 6 seconds, how long is the second train?
questions.explanation: The combined speed is 30 m/s. Multiply by the passing time to get both lengths together and subtract the length of the first train.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A total of 66 tickets cost ₹2055. Regular tickets cost ₹40 and concession tickets cost ₹25. How many regular tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Subtract what all concession tickets would cost from the actual total, then divide the difference by ₹15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A waiting hall has 14 rows. The first row has 13 seats and each subsequent row has 3 more. How many seats are in the last four rows together?
questions.explanation: The last four rows have L, L−3, L−6 and L−9 seats, where L is the final row count.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A status display refreshes every 12 min and a timer every 18 min. Both refresh at 08:00. How many minutes after 08:00 do they refresh together for the third time, excluding 08:00?
questions.explanation: The joint period is LCM(4k,6k) = 12k, with k = 3. The third joint refresh is after three such periods.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: There are 7 red and 10 blue tokens. Two are sampled without replacement. What is the probability of sampling two reds, to three decimals?
questions.explanation: Multiply the probability of a red first by the conditional probability of another red after one has been removed.

questions.explanation: Each replacement earns an extra ₹(35−20), or ₹15. Multiply by 15 replacements.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Counters P and Q sold 136 tickets together. How many did P sell? I. P sold 6 more than Q. II. P sold more than 40 tickets.
questions.explanation: The total and exact difference determine P. A lower bound alone leaves several possible counts.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A service by Chittoor has a total of 300 seats in two coaches. How many seats does coach A have? I. A has more seats than B. II. B has exactly 115 seats.
questions.explanation: Subtract the known B count from the total. Knowing only which is larger does not determine the count.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A dispatcher at Chittoor sees two queues. Is the service rate of X higher than that of Y? I. X serves three times as many people. II. X takes twice as long for that number. Both counts are positive.
questions.explanation: The rate comparison needs both the count ratio and the time ratio. Together they give X at 1.5 times Y.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three docks dispatched 33, 43, and 53 parcels in some order. B dispatched more than C. A did not dispatch the fewest or the most. What was B’s count?
questions.explanation: A must be the middle dock. Of the remaining two, B is larger.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three weekly totals average 83. The first two were 68 and 93. What was the final total?
questions.explanation: Multiply the mean by three, then subtract the two known observations.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Chittoor, two switches start open. An indicator turns on exactly when one switch is closed. The first switch is now closed and the indicator is off. What follows?
questions.explanation: With the first switch closed, an open second switch would turn the indicator on.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: The rule at Chittoor states that each accepted request has a reference number. Request 33 has no reference number. What can be concluded?
options: The request was accepted with a special code.
All requests without account IDs are accepted.
questions.explanation: An accepted request necessarily has a reference number. Its absence rules out acceptance.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 5:08?
questions.explanation: The minute hand is at 48°. The hour hand is at 154°. Take the smaller angular separation.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A review at Chittoor was held on Thursday. What weekday is the next review if it is 60 days later?
questions.explanation: The day shift is the remainder when 60 is divided by seven.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Charu is the sister of Farah. Farah is the mother of Jaya. How is Charu related to Jaya?
questions.explanation: The person described is the sister of the child’s mother.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What negates the claim “Every consignment checked at Chittoor was both tagged and sealed”?
options: Every checked consignment was untagged and unsealed.
Some checked consignments were both tagged and sealed.
At least one checked consignment was untagged or unsealed.
questions.explanation: To refute the universal claim, one checked consignment need only fail either requirement.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Chittoor, exactly two tasks are selected from A, B, C and D. Choosing A requires C. Tasks B and C cannot both be selected. Which pair is valid?
questions.explanation: The pair includes A’s prerequisite and avoids the prohibited combination.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Some enquiries at Chittoor are forwarded. Every forwarded enquiry receives a tracking number. Some enquiries are urgent. What is certain?
options: Every enquiry with a tracking number is urgent.
No enquiry with a tracking number is urgent.
questions.explanation: At least one forwarded enquiry exists, and every forwarded enquiry receives a number. Urgency is unrelated in the premises.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Only one of Charu, Farah and Jaya signed a receipt. Charu says that Farah signed it. Farah says that Jaya signed it. Jaya says that Farah did not sign it. Exactly two statements are true. Who signed it?
questions.explanation: The statements by the first and third people are complements. The middle statement must be true as well.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A box may leave shelf 43 only when it has passed inspection and has a collection code. A box has passed inspection and lacks a collection code. What follows?
options: It may not leave under this rule.
It necessarily belongs to another shelf.
questions.explanation: Passing inspection meets one requirement. A collection code is also required.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Surveyors at Chittoor interviewed only passengers who arrived before 08:00. Most interviewed passengers favoured a morning service. Which conclusion is defensible?
options: Most passengers at all hours favoured the service.
Most members of the interviewed group favoured the service.
The survey sampled all types of passengers equally.
questions.explanation: The survey supports a statement about its sample. The time restriction limits broader inference.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Chittoor, a form is accepted whenever its two signatures are present. A particular form was not accepted. What must follow?
options: At least one signature was absent.
The form was accepted without a signature.
questions.explanation: If both signatures were present, the rule would guarantee acceptance. Nonacceptance rules out both being present.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: During review 13, case P is earlier than Q. R is earlier than P and S is later than Q. Which case is third in time order?
questions.explanation: The constraints force R, P, Q, S in that order.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Chittoor, all inspected consignments are tagged. No tagged consignment is in bay Z. Some priority consignments are inspected. Which conclusion is forced?
options: Some priority consignments are outside bay Z.
Some inspected consignments are in bay Z.
Every consignment outside bay Z is tagged.
questions.explanation: An inspected priority consignment is tagged and therefore outside bay Z.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An office in Chittoor moves a help desk next to the numbered gates to cut requests for directions. Which assumption is needed?
options: All visitors prefer speaking to an official.
The desk handles refunds at every gate.
The number of gates will decrease.
Some people needing directions can find the relocated desk.
questions.explanation: For the relocation to affect direction requests, at least some intended users must be able to reach the desk.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: After a digital guide was installed at Chittoor, missed connections fell. Which observation most weakens the argument that the guide caused the reduction?
options: The guide uses larger text than the old notice.
The timetable simultaneously lengthened the connection windows.
The total number of express routes remained steady.
Users consulted the guide on both weekdays and weekends.
questions.explanation: More time to connect is an alternative explanation that changed when the guide changed.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What makes the first museum comparison difficult to interpret?
options: The museum did not install captions anywhere.
Visitors were forbidden to read technical details.
The curator recorded only exit ticket sales.
Caption design and exhibit location differed at the same time.
questions.explanation: Time near an entrance can differ for reasons unrelated to caption design.
questions.passage: A museum tested captions that began with a short description followed by optional technical detail. Visitors paused longer at several exhibits, but the new captions were placed near the entrance, where visitors often slowed down anyway. For the next trial, the curator plans to alternate the two caption designs at the same exhibits on comparable days.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: How does the proposed trial improve the comparison?
options: It compares both designs at the same exhibits across similar days.
It moves all exhibits farther from the entrance.
It removes descriptions from both designs.
It counts only visitors who have previously visited.
questions.explanation: Using the same exhibits holds location and exhibit content more nearly constant.
questions.passage: A museum tested captions that began with a short description followed by optional technical detail. Visitors paused longer at several exhibits, but the new captions were placed near the entrance, where visitors often slowed down anyway. questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What feature of the revised caption serves a reader who wants more information?
options: The position of the exhibit near the entrance.
The schedule used for comparable days.
The optional technical detail after the first description.
The measured length of other visitors’ pauses.
questions.explanation: Readers may go beyond the brief opening to the technical material.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which claim about visitor pauses can be made from the first trial alone?
options: Longer pauses prove every visitor understood the exhibits.
Every entrance exhibit recorded the same time.
Technical readers disliked the short description.
Some revised-caption exhibits recorded longer pauses.
questions.explanation: The passage reports the observed change without establishing understanding or its cause.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person is 13th from the front of a 42-person queue. What is their rank from the back, counting the person?
questions.explanation: Subtract the front rank from the total and add one.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A runner was 11th from the end. After 6 entrants finish behind the runner and two ahead, what is their new rank from the end?
questions.explanation: Only finishers behind the runner increase their rank from the end.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The pair 8 : 80 follows a rule: square the first number and add twice the first number. What pairs with 10?
questions.explanation: Apply n²+2n to 10.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A two-digit number is coded as three times its tens digit plus twice its units digit. What is the code for 27?
questions.explanation: Read the tens and units digits separately and apply the two stated weights.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: There are 8 assignments. Two designated assignments must be consecutive, in either order. If just their leftmost starting slot and their internal order are counted, how many placements are possible?
questions.explanation: The consecutive pair can start in any slot except the last and has two orientations.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person walks 18 m west, then 6 m east and 9 m north. What is the distance from the start?
questions.explanation: The net legs are 4k west and 3k north, so the straight-line distance is the 5k hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In file batch 53, A sits left of B; D immediately follows B; C is first and E is last. What is third in the order?
questions.explanation: After fixing the ends, the three middle positions can only be A, B, D.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In team Chittoor, P scored higher than Q and R. Q scored higher than S but lower than R. Who placed second?
questions.explanation: The four place in descending order P, R, Q, S.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Fill the blank in 6, 11, …, 21, 26.
questions.explanation: The arithmetic progression increases by five.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Apply the same rule as the sequence 3, 6, 18, 36, 108 to find the next term.
questions.explanation: The multipliers alternate between 2 and 3. After ×3 comes ×2.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The quantities 7 and 21 are paired. Applying the same ratio to 12 gives what paired number?
questions.explanation: The second quantity in the example is three times the first.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: At Chittoor, five counters line up in a fixed list. Counter A must come first and counter E last. How many possible orders of the remaining counters meet the requirement that B is before C?
questions.explanation: Of the 3! orders of the middle counters, exactly half have B before C.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Which of these proposed pairs for block 3 fails the rule that the second letter is two alphabet positions after the first, with wraparound?
questions.explanation: The failing pair moves by three positions. The other three move by two.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A number has 1 as its tens digit and 4 as its units digit. What is the difference between the reversed number and the original?
questions.explanation: Swapping digits changes the number by nine times their difference, which is 3.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 6, 11, 21, 36, 56, …
questions.explanation: Differences are successive multiples of 5. The next difference is 25.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 6, 18, 16, 48, 46, …
questions.explanation: Apply ×3 and −2 alternately. The next operation is ×3.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete 5, 43, 9, 40, 13, 37, …
questions.explanation: Odd positions increase by four, while even positions decrease by three. The next position is odd.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: What pair follows SG, RH, PJ, MM, …? The alphabet wraps around.
questions.explanation: The first letter moves backwards and the second forwards by 1, 2, 3 and then 4 places.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: How is CHITT coded if letters in odd positions advance one place and letters in even positions move back two places, wrapping when necessary?
questions.explanation: Apply the alternating shifts independently to each letter. The transformed letters are D, F, J, R, U.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Encode CHITT by moving every letter back one place and then reversing the result. The letter before A is Z.
questions.explanation: First substitute the preceding letter for each character, then read the substituted word backwards.

title: RRB Station Master CBT · Practice model 7
note: A full-length paper with newly parameterised calculations, charts, data sufficiency, comprehension and reasoning. It follows the indicative 30/30/20/20 breakdown.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A metal sheet measures 16 cm by 25 cm and is 4 mm thick. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Convert the thickness to 0.4 cm. Multiplying it by the base area gives 10 times the first side length.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 48 cm³ sample of density 3 g/cm³ is combined with a 32 cm³ sample of density 5 g/cm³ without volume change. What is their combined density?
questions.explanation: The mass is 36k+40k = 76k g and the volume is 20k cm³, where k = 4. Divide to obtain the density.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A component has a mass of 9 kg. What is the decrease in weight when moved from a location with g = 10 m/s² to one with g = 8 m/s²?
questions.explanation: Mass stays constant. Weight changes by the mass times the 2 m/s² difference in g.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 9 kg trolley is pulled east by 63 N and west by 36 N. It starts at rest. How far does it travel in 4 s if the forces are constant?
questions.explanation: The net force is 3 times the mass, giving 3 m/s² east. From rest, distance = ½×3×4².

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A sliding crate is pulled with a horizontal force of 90 N along 8 m. Kinetic friction is 30 N. What is the net work on the crate?
questions.explanation: Only horizontal forces do work here. Their net value is twice the friction force in the direction of travel.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 9 kg object slows from 8 m/s to 4 m/s. Find the magnitude of net work done during braking.
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the kinetic energy decrease is ½m(8²−4²) = 24m.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A lift raises a 45 kg load by 3 m in 6 s at a steady speed. Take g = 10 m/s² and efficiency 75%. What input power is needed to the nearest watt?
questions.explanation: Useful power is (5m)×10×3/6 = 125m watts. Divide by 0.75 to find the input power.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 245 N load acts 20 cm to the left of a frictionless pivot. A 35 N load counterbalances it on the right. What is the right-hand lever arm?
questions.explanation: For equilibrium the moments are equal. The smaller force must have 7 times the lever arm.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Resistors of 6 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in series to 36 V. What power is delivered to the larger resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance is 18 Ω. The series current is 2 A, so the larger resistor receives I²R = 4×12.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two 12 Ω resistors are connected in parallel to 36 V. One branch opens. How much does the current drawn from the source decrease?
questions.explanation: Each connected branch draws V/R = 3 A. Disconnecting one branch removes its 3 A contribution.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 2 kW appliance runs for 48 min each day for 10 days. What is its electricity cost at ₹6.50/kWh?
questions.explanation: Forty-eight minutes is 0.8 hour. Multiply power by 8 hours total and then by ₹6.50/kWh.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Mix 400 g of water at 75°C with 1200 g at 15°C in an insulated vessel of negligible heat capacity. What is the equilibrium temperature?
questions.explanation: The cooler water has triple the mass. The weighted mean is (75+3×15)/4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A heater transfers 3600 J of energy into a 0.4 kg metal block. If the temperature rises by 15°C, find the block’s specific heat capacity.
questions.explanation: Use c=Q/(mΔT), which gives 3600 divided by 0.4×15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A linear sensor reads 4 units at 0°C and 108 units at 100°C. What is the reading at 40°C, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: Add 40% of the change from zero to boiling to the sensor’s reading at 0°C.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An ideal pulley system has four rope segments supporting a 240 N load. What is the work done at the free end to raise the load 1.5 m?
questions.explanation: In an ideal machine the input work equals the increase in potential energy: weight × height.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The ordered measurements are 4, 7, 10, 12, 14, 19, 24. The smallest is corrected to 29. What is the new median?
questions.explanation: The corrected value moves to the end. The old fifth observation becomes the new fourth observation.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A workshop pays a fixed fee of ₹89 plus ₹7 per unit. It pays ₹355 total. What would the bill have been if it had used 6 fewer units?
questions.explanation: The fee is unchanged. Subtract 6×₹7 from the original bill.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two adjacent interior angles of a parallelogram differ by 8°. What is the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles sum to 180°. The larger is 90° plus half their stated difference.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A depot marks a spare part at ₹1500. It applies discounts of 20% and then 15%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: Multiply the marked price by 0.8×0.85 = 0.68. The second discount applies to the reduced price.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: After selling 30% of its ticket stock, a depot has 154 tickets. How many would remain if it then sold one-seventh of the remaining tickets?
questions.explanation: The second sale leaves six-sevenths of 154. The original stock is unnecessary for this step.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The mean mass of 18 sacks is 41 kg. Four other sacks averaging 47 kg are added. What is the combined mean to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: Add the two total masses before dividing by the new number of sacks.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: P can complete a task in 24 days and Q in 48 days. They work together for 4 days. How many more days does Q need alone?
questions.explanation: Together they complete k(1/(6k)+1/(12k)) = one-quarter. Q completes the remaining three-quarters in 9k days. Here k = 4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 168 m train travels at 72 km/h and passes a second train moving towards it at 36 km/h. If the entire pass takes 7 seconds, how long is the second train?
questions.explanation: The combined speed is 30 m/s. Multiply by the passing time to get both lengths together and subtract the length of the first train.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A total of 78 tickets cost ₹2430. Regular tickets cost ₹40 and concession tickets cost ₹25. How many regular tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Subtract what all concession tickets would cost from the actual total, then divide the difference by ₹15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A waiting hall has 16 rows. The first row has 13 seats and each subsequent row has 3 more. How many seats are in the last four rows together?
questions.explanation: The last four rows have L, L−3, L−6 and L−9 seats, where L is the final row count.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A status display refreshes every 16 min and a timer every 24 min. Both refresh at 08:00. How many minutes after 08:00 do they refresh together for the third time, excluding 08:00?
questions.explanation: The joint period is LCM(4k,6k) = 12k, with k = 4. The third joint refresh is after three such periods.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: There are 8 red and 11 blue tokens. Two are sampled without replacement. What is the probability of sampling two reds, to three decimals?
questions.explanation: Multiply the probability of a red first by the conditional probability of another red after one has been removed.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The water level in a cuboid tank of base 20 cm by 24 cm rises from 7 cm to 14 cm when an object is fully submerged. What is the object’s volume?
questions.explanation: The object displaces the base area multiplied by the rise in water level.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A circular island of radius 8 m is surrounded by a walkway 3 m wide. What is the walkway area, in multiples of π?
questions.explanation: Subtract the inner disk from the outer disk: (r+3)²−r² = 6r+9.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 12 m vertical pole casts a 16 m shadow. From the shadow tip what is the cosine of the angle of elevation?
questions.explanation: The right triangle is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle. Cosine is the horizontal side over the hypotenuse.
