questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Counters P and Q sold 148 tickets together. How many did P sell? I. P sold 8 more than Q. II. P sold more than 40 tickets.
questions.explanation: The total and exact difference determine P. A lower bound alone leaves several possible counts.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A service by Dharmavaram has a total of 320 seats in two coaches. How many seats does coach A have? I. A has more seats than B. II. B has exactly 120 seats.
questions.explanation: Subtract the known B count from the total. Knowing only which is larger does not determine the count.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A dispatcher at Dharmavaram sees two queues. Is the service rate of X higher than that of Y? I. X serves three times as many people. II. X takes twice as long for that number. Both counts are positive.
questions.explanation: The rate comparison needs both the count ratio and the time ratio. Together they give X at 1.5 times Y.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three docks dispatched 34, 44, and 54 parcels in some order. B dispatched more than C. A did not dispatch the fewest or the most. What was B’s count?
questions.explanation: A must be the middle dock. Of the remaining two, B is larger.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three weekly totals average 84. The first two were 69 and 94. What was the final total?
questions.explanation: Multiply the mean by three, then subtract the two known observations.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: The rule at Dharmavaram states that each accepted request has a reference number. Request 34 has no reference number. What can be concluded?
options: The request was accepted with a special code.
All requests without account IDs are accepted.
questions.explanation: An accepted request necessarily has a reference number. Its absence rules out acceptance.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 6:09?
questions.explanation: The minute hand is at 54°. The hour hand is at 184.5°. Take the smaller angular separation.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A review at Dharmavaram was held on Friday. What weekday is the next review if it is 64 days later?
questions.explanation: The day shift is the remainder when 64 is divided by seven.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Deepa is the sister of Gita. Gita is the mother of Kiran. How is Deepa related to Kiran?
questions.explanation: The person described is the sister of the child’s mother.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What negates the claim “Every consignment checked at Dharmavaram was both tagged and sealed”?
options: Every checked consignment was untagged and unsealed.
At least one checked consignment was untagged or unsealed.
Some checked consignments were both tagged and sealed.
questions.explanation: To refute the universal claim, one checked consignment need only fail either requirement.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Dharmavaram, exactly two tasks are selected from A, B, C and D. Choosing A requires C. Tasks B and C cannot both be selected. Which pair is valid?
questions.explanation: The pair includes A’s prerequisite and avoids the prohibited combination.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Some enquiries at Dharmavaram are forwarded. Every forwarded enquiry receives a tracking number. Some enquiries are urgent. What is certain?
options: Every enquiry with a tracking number is urgent.
No enquiry with a tracking number is urgent.
questions.explanation: At least one forwarded enquiry exists, and every forwarded enquiry receives a number. Urgency is unrelated in the premises.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Only one of Deepa, Gita and Kiran signed a receipt. Deepa says that Gita signed it. Gita says that Kiran signed it. Kiran says that Gita did not sign it. Exactly two statements are true. Who signed it?
questions.explanation: The statements by the first and third people are complements. The middle statement must be true as well.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A box may leave shelf 44 only when it has passed inspection and has a collection code. A box has passed inspection and lacks a collection code. What follows?
options: It may not leave under this rule.
It necessarily belongs to another shelf.
questions.explanation: Passing inspection meets one requirement. A collection code is also required.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Surveyors at Dharmavaram interviewed only passengers who arrived before 08:00. Most interviewed passengers favoured a morning service. Which conclusion is defensible?
options: Most passengers at all hours favoured the service.
Most members of the interviewed group favoured the service.
The survey sampled all types of passengers equally.
questions.explanation: The survey supports a statement about its sample. The time restriction limits broader inference.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Dharmavaram, a form is accepted whenever its two signatures are present. A particular form was not accepted. What must follow?
options: At least one signature was absent.
The form was accepted without a signature.
questions.explanation: If both signatures were present, the rule would guarantee acceptance. Nonacceptance rules out both being present.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: During review 14, case P is earlier than Q. R is earlier than P and S is later than Q. Which case is third in time order?
questions.explanation: The constraints force R, P, Q, S in that order.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Dharmavaram, all inspected consignments are tagged. No tagged consignment is in bay Z. Some priority consignments are inspected. Which conclusion is forced?
options: Some priority consignments are outside bay Z.
Some inspected consignments are in bay Z.
Every consignment outside bay Z is tagged.
questions.explanation: An inspected priority consignment is tagged and therefore outside bay Z.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An office in Dharmavaram moves a help desk next to the numbered gates to cut requests for directions. Which assumption is needed?
options: Some people needing directions can find the relocated desk.
All visitors prefer speaking to an official.
The desk handles refunds at every gate.
The number of gates will decrease.
questions.explanation: For the relocation to affect direction requests, at least some intended users must be able to reach the desk.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: After a digital guide was installed at Dharmavaram, missed connections fell. Which observation most weakens the argument that the guide caused the reduction?
options: The timetable simultaneously lengthened the connection windows.
The guide uses larger text than the old notice.
The total number of express routes remained steady.
Users consulted the guide on both weekdays and weekends.
questions.explanation: More time to connect is an alternative explanation that changed when the guide changed.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Dharmavaram, two switches start open. An indicator turns on exactly when one switch is closed. The first switch is now closed and the indicator is off. What follows?
questions.explanation: With the first switch closed, an open second switch would turn the indicator on.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What prompted the manager to add a second measure?
options: Every supplier delivered more crates than expected.
The closing time moved earlier each day.
The market stopped scheduling delivery slots.
The supply volume changed, affecting the meaning of the raw backlog count.
questions.explanation: A smaller backlog can arise from fewer deliveries even if processing is unchanged.
questions.passage: A market replaced a single long delivery window with three scheduled slots. The number of crates waiting at closing time fell. The manager also noticed that some suppliers had begun sending fewer crates because of seasonal changes. She decided to track the share of delivered crates processed by closing, alongside the count of crates waiting.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What denominator applies to the new measure?
questions.explanation: The new measure is the proportion of delivered crates processed by closing.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What is the strongest sign that processing improved on the new schedule?
options: Fewer crates were delivered during the off-season.
Suppliers used a larger variety of labels.
The market has exactly three slots.
The share processed rose on days with comparable deliveries.
questions.explanation: Improved completion at comparable load supports a change in performance.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which distinction is central to the manager’s decision?
options: The difference between morning and evening seasons.
The difference between supplier names and customer names.

The difference between the size and colour of crates.
questions.explanation: A raw backlog and a rate can move differently when total volume changes.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The pair 9 : 99 follows a rule: square the first number and add twice the first number. What pairs with 11?
questions.explanation: Apply n²+2n to 11.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A two-digit number is coded as three times its tens digit plus twice its units digit. What is the code for 28?
questions.explanation: Read the tens and units digits separately and apply the two stated weights.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: There are 9 assignments. Two designated assignments must be consecutive, in either order. If just their leftmost starting slot and their internal order are counted, how many placements are possible?
questions.explanation: The consecutive pair can start in any slot except the last and has two orientations.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person walks 24 m west, then 8 m east and 12 m north. What is the distance from the start?
questions.explanation: The net legs are 4k west and 3k north, so the straight-line distance is the 5k hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In file batch 54, A sits left of B; D immediately follows B; C is first and E is last. What is third in the order?
questions.explanation: After fixing the ends, the three middle positions can only be A, B, D.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In team Dharmavaram, P scored higher than Q and R. Q scored higher than S but lower than R. Who placed second?
questions.explanation: The four place in descending order P, R, Q, S.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Fill the blank in 7, 12, …, 22, 27.
questions.explanation: The arithmetic progression increases by five.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Apply the same rule as the sequence 4, 8, 24, 48, 144 to find the next term.
questions.explanation: The multipliers alternate between 2 and 3. After ×3 comes ×2.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The quantities 8 and 24 are paired. Applying the same ratio to 13 gives what paired number?
questions.explanation: The second quantity in the example is three times the first.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: At Dharmavaram, five counters line up in a fixed list. Counter A must come first and counter E last. How many possible orders of the remaining counters meet the requirement that B is before C?
questions.explanation: Of the 3! orders of the middle counters, exactly half have B before C.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Which of these proposed pairs for block 4 fails the rule that the second letter is two alphabet positions after the first, with wraparound?
questions.explanation: The failing pair moves by three positions. The other three move by two.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A number has 1 as its tens digit and 5 as its units digit. What is the difference between the reversed number and the original?
questions.explanation: Swapping digits changes the number by nine times their difference, which is 4.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 7, 9, 13, 19, 27, …
questions.explanation: Differences are successive multiples of 2. The next difference is 10.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 7, 21, 19, 57, 55, …
questions.explanation: Apply ×3 and −2 alternately. The next operation is ×3.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete 6, 44, 10, 41, 14, 38, …
questions.explanation: Odd positions increase by four, while even positions decrease by three. The next position is odd.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: What pair follows TH, SI, QK, NN, …? The alphabet wraps around.
questions.explanation: The first letter moves backwards and the second forwards by 1, 2, 3 and then 4 places.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: How is DHARM coded if letters in odd positions advance one place and letters in even positions move back two places, wrapping when necessary?
questions.explanation: Apply the alternating shifts independently to each letter. The transformed letters are E, F, B, P, N.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Encode DHARM by moving every letter back one place and then reversing the result. The letter before A is Z.
questions.explanation: First substitute the preceding letter for each character, then read the substituted word backwards.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person is 14th from the front of a 44-person queue. What is their rank from the back, counting the person?
questions.explanation: Subtract the front rank from the total and add one.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A runner was 12th from the end. After 7 entrants finish behind the runner and two ahead, what is their new rank from the end?
questions.explanation: Only finishers behind the runner increase their rank from the end.

title: RRB Station Master CBT · Practice model 8
note: A full-length paper with newly parameterised calculations, charts, data sufficiency, comprehension and reasoning. It follows the indicative 30/30/20/20 breakdown.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 10 kg trolley is pulled east by 70 N and west by 40 N. It starts at rest. How far does it travel in 4 s if the forces are constant?
questions.explanation: The net force is 3 times the mass, giving 3 m/s² east. From rest, distance = ½×3×4².

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A sliding crate is pulled with a horizontal force of 105 N along 9 m. Kinetic friction is 35 N. What is the net work on the crate?
questions.explanation: Only horizontal forces do work here. Their net value is twice the friction force in the direction of travel.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 10 kg object slows from 8 m/s to 4 m/s. Find the magnitude of net work done during braking.
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the kinetic energy decrease is ½m(8²−4²) = 24m.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A lift raises a 50 kg load by 3 m in 6 s at a steady speed. Take g = 10 m/s² and efficiency 75%. What input power is needed to the nearest watt?
questions.explanation: Useful power is (5m)×10×3/6 = 125m watts. Divide by 0.75 to find the input power.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 288 N load acts 20 cm to the left of a frictionless pivot. A 36 N load counterbalances it on the right. What is the right-hand lever arm?
questions.explanation: For equilibrium the moments are equal. The smaller force must have 8 times the lever arm.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Resistors of 7 Ω and 14 Ω are connected in series to 42 V. What power is delivered to the larger resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance is 21 Ω. The series current is 2 A, so the larger resistor receives I²R = 4×14.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two 14 Ω resistors are connected in parallel to 42 V. One branch opens. How much does the current drawn from the source decrease?
questions.explanation: Each connected branch draws V/R = 3 A. Disconnecting one branch removes its 3 A contribution.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 2.25 kW appliance runs for 48 min each day for 10 days. What is its electricity cost at ₹6.50/kWh?
questions.explanation: Forty-eight minutes is 0.8 hour. Multiply power by 8 hours total and then by ₹6.50/kWh.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Mix 500 g of water at 75°C with 1500 g at 15°C in an insulated vessel of negligible heat capacity. What is the equilibrium temperature?
questions.explanation: The cooler water has triple the mass. The weighted mean is (75+3×15)/4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A heater transfers 4500 J of energy into a 0.5 kg metal block. If the temperature rises by 15°C, find the block’s specific heat capacity.
questions.explanation: Use c=Q/(mΔT), which gives 4500 divided by 0.5×15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A linear sensor reads 5 units at 0°C and 110 units at 100°C. What is the reading at 40°C, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: Add 40% of the change from zero to boiling to the sensor’s reading at 0°C.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An ideal pulley system has four rope segments supporting a 300 N load. What is the work done at the free end to raise the load 1.5 m?
questions.explanation: In an ideal machine the input work equals the increase in potential energy: weight × height.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The ordered measurements are 5, 8, 11, 13, 15, 20, 25. The smallest is corrected to 30. What is the new median?
questions.explanation: The corrected value moves to the end. The old fifth observation becomes the new fourth observation.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A workshop pays a fixed fee of ₹90 plus ₹7 per unit. It pays ₹370 total. What would the bill have been if it had used 6 fewer units?
questions.explanation: The fee is unchanged. Subtract 6×₹7 from the original bill.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two adjacent interior angles of a parallelogram differ by 10°. What is the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles sum to 180°. The larger is 90° plus half their stated difference.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A depot marks a spare part at ₹1600. It applies discounts of 20% and then 15%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: Multiply the marked price by 0.8×0.85 = 0.68. The second discount applies to the reduced price.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: After selling 30% of its ticket stock, a depot has 161 tickets. How many would remain if it then sold one-seventh of the remaining tickets?
questions.explanation: The second sale leaves six-sevenths of 161. The original stock is unnecessary for this step.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The mean mass of 20 sacks is 41 kg. Four other sacks averaging 48 kg are added. What is the combined mean to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: Add the two total masses before dividing by the new number of sacks.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: P can complete a task in 30 days and Q in 60 days. They work together for 5 days. How many more days does Q need alone?
questions.explanation: Together they complete k(1/(6k)+1/(12k)) = one-quarter. Q completes the remaining three-quarters in 9k days. Here k = 5.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 192 m train travels at 72 km/h and passes a second train moving towards it at 36 km/h. If the entire pass takes 8 seconds, how long is the second train?
questions.explanation: The combined speed is 30 m/s. Multiply by the passing time to get both lengths together and subtract the length of the first train.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A total of 90 tickets cost ₹2805. Regular tickets cost ₹40 and concession tickets cost ₹25. How many regular tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Subtract what all concession tickets would cost from the actual total, then divide the difference by ₹15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A waiting hall has 18 rows. The first row has 13 seats and each subsequent row has 3 more. How many seats are in the last four rows together?
questions.explanation: The last four rows have L, L−3, L−6 and L−9 seats, where L is the final row count.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A status display refreshes every 20 min and a timer every 30 min. Both refresh at 08:00. How many minutes after 08:00 do they refresh together for the third time, excluding 08:00?
questions.explanation: The joint period is LCM(4k,6k) = 12k, with k = 5. The third joint refresh is after three such periods.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: There are 9 red and 12 blue tokens. Two are sampled without replacement. What is the probability of sampling two reds, to three decimals?
questions.explanation: Multiply the probability of a red first by the conditional probability of another red after one has been removed.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The water level in a cuboid tank of base 25 cm by 24 cm rises from 7 cm to 15 cm when an object is fully submerged. What is the object’s volume?
questions.explanation: The object displaces the base area multiplied by the rise in water level.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A circular island of radius 9 m is surrounded by a walkway 3 m wide. What is the walkway area, in multiples of π?
questions.explanation: Subtract the inner disk from the outer disk: (r+3)²−r² = 6r+9.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 15 m vertical pole casts a 20 m shadow. From the shadow tip what is the cosine of the angle of elevation?
questions.explanation: The right triangle is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle. Cosine is the horizontal side over the hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A metal sheet measures 17 cm by 25 cm and is 4 mm thick. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Convert the thickness to 0.4 cm. Multiplying it by the base area gives 10 times the first side length.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 60 cm³ sample of density 3 g/cm³ is combined with a 40 cm³ sample of density 5 g/cm³ without volume change. What is their combined density?
questions.explanation: The mass is 36k+40k = 76k g and the volume is 20k cm³, where k = 5. Divide to obtain the density.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A component has a mass of 10 kg. What is the decrease in weight when moved from a location with g = 10 m/s² to one with g = 8 m/s²?
questions.explanation: Mass stays constant. Weight changes by the mass times the 2 m/s² difference in g.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Counters P and Q sold 160 tickets together. How many did P sell? I. P sold 10 more than Q. II. P sold more than 40 tickets.
questions.explanation: The total and exact difference determine P. A lower bound alone leaves several possible counts.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A service by Eluru has a total of 340 seats in two coaches. How many seats does coach A have? I. A has more seats than B. II. B has exactly 125 seats.
questions.explanation: Subtract the known B count from the total. Knowing only which is larger does not determine the count.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A dispatcher at Eluru sees two queues. Is the service rate of X higher than that of Y? I. X serves three times as many people. II. X takes twice as long for that number. Both counts are positive.
questions.explanation: The rate comparison needs both the count ratio and the time ratio. Together they give X at 1.5 times Y.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three docks dispatched 35, 45, and 55 parcels in some order. B dispatched more than C. A did not dispatch the fewest or the most. What was B’s count?
questions.explanation: A must be the middle dock. Of the remaining two, B is larger.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three weekly totals average 85. The first two were 70 and 95. What was the final total?
questions.explanation: Multiply the mean by three, then subtract the two known observations.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 2:10?
questions.explanation: The minute hand is at 60°. The hour hand is at 65°. Take the smaller angular separation.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A review at Eluru was held on Saturday. What weekday is the next review if it is 68 days later?
questions.explanation: The day shift is the remainder when 68 is divided by seven.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Esha is the sister of Hema. Hema is the mother of Lata. How is Esha related to Lata?
questions.explanation: The person described is the sister of the child’s mother.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What negates the claim “Every consignment checked at Eluru was both tagged and sealed”?
options: Every checked consignment was untagged and unsealed.
Some checked consignments were both tagged and sealed.
At least one checked consignment was untagged or unsealed.
questions.explanation: To refute the universal claim, one checked consignment need only fail either requirement.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Eluru, exactly two tasks are selected from A, B, C and D. Choosing A requires C. Tasks B and C cannot both be selected. Which pair is valid?
questions.explanation: The pair includes A’s prerequisite and avoids the prohibited combination.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Some enquiries at Eluru are forwarded. Every forwarded enquiry receives a tracking number. Some enquiries are urgent. What is certain?
options: Every enquiry with a tracking number is urgent.
No enquiry with a tracking number is urgent.
questions.explanation: At least one forwarded enquiry exists, and every forwarded enquiry receives a number. Urgency is unrelated in the premises.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Only one of Esha, Hema and Lata signed a receipt. Esha says that Hema signed it. Hema says that Lata signed it. Lata says that Hema did not sign it. Exactly two statements are true. Who signed it?
questions.explanation: The statements by the first and third people are complements. The middle statement must be true as well.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A box may leave shelf 45 only when it has passed inspection and has a collection code. A box has passed inspection and lacks a collection code. What follows?
options: It may not leave under this rule.
It necessarily belongs to another shelf.
questions.explanation: Passing inspection meets one requirement. A collection code is also required.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Surveyors at Eluru interviewed only passengers who arrived before 08:00. Most interviewed passengers favoured a morning service. Which conclusion is defensible?
options: Most members of the interviewed group favoured the service.
Most passengers at all hours favoured the service.
The survey sampled all types of passengers equally.
questions.explanation: The survey supports a statement about its sample. The time restriction limits broader inference.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Eluru, a form is accepted whenever its two signatures are present. A particular form was not accepted. What must follow?
options: The form was accepted without a signature.
At least one signature was absent.
questions.explanation: If both signatures were present, the rule would guarantee acceptance. Nonacceptance rules out both being present.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: During review 15, case P is earlier than Q. R is earlier than P and S is later than Q. Which case is third in time order?
questions.explanation: The constraints force R, P, Q, S in that order.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Eluru, all inspected consignments are tagged. No tagged consignment is in bay Z. Some priority consignments are inspected. Which conclusion is forced?
options: Some inspected consignments are in bay Z.
Every consignment outside bay Z is tagged.
Some priority consignments are outside bay Z.
questions.explanation: An inspected priority consignment is tagged and therefore outside bay Z.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An office in Eluru moves a help desk next to the numbered gates to cut requests for directions. Which assumption is needed?
options: All visitors prefer speaking to an official.
The desk handles refunds at every gate.
Some people needing directions can find the relocated desk.
The number of gates will decrease.
questions.explanation: For the relocation to affect direction requests, at least some intended users must be able to reach the desk.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: After a digital guide was installed at Eluru, missed connections fell. Which observation most weakens the argument that the guide caused the reduction?
options: The guide uses larger text than the old notice.
The total number of express routes remained steady.
The timetable simultaneously lengthened the connection windows.
Users consulted the guide on both weekdays and weekends.
questions.explanation: More time to connect is an alternative explanation that changed when the guide changed.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Eluru, two switches start open. An indicator turns on exactly when one switch is closed. The first switch is now closed and the indicator is off. What follows?
questions.explanation: With the first switch closed, an open second switch would turn the indicator on.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: The rule at Eluru states that each accepted request has a reference number. Request 35 has no reference number. What can be concluded?
options: The request was accepted with a special code.
All requests without account IDs are accepted.
questions.explanation: An accepted request necessarily has a reference number. Its absence rules out acceptance.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which aspect of the original butterfly counts threatens comparability?
options: The same species of shrub was used on both routes.
Time and weather differed between routes.
Several volunteers helped collect the counts.
questions.explanation: Weather and time can alter which butterflies are visible independently of the shrubs.
questions.passage: A citizen group planted native shrubs alongside two walking routes. A later count found more butterflies on one route. Counters on that route visited on calm afternoons, whereas the other route was surveyed in windy mornings. The group plans to rotate volunteers between routes and count at matched times and weather conditions.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Why rotate the survey volunteers?
options: It guarantees identical plants will grow everywhere.
It reduces the chance that differences between observers are always associated with one route.
It prevents butterflies from changing routes.
It removes the need to record weather.
questions.explanation: Rotating volunteers reduces systematic differences caused by one observer always counting one route.
questions.passage: A citizen group planted native shrubs alongside two walking routes. A later count found more butterflies on one route. Counters on that route visited on calm afternoons, whereas the other route was surveyed in windy mornings. The group plans to rotate volunteers between routes and count at matched times and weather conditions.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What does the passage establish about the first comparison?
options: One route recorded more butterflies under its survey conditions.
The planting increased butterfly abundance everywhere.
Windy mornings always have fewer butterflies.
The volunteers counted every butterfly present.
questions.explanation: The first comparison establishes the observed difference under different survey conditions.
questions.passage: A citizen group planted native shrubs alongside two walking routes. A later count found more butterflies on one route. Counters on that route visited on calm afternoons, whereas the other route was surveyed in windy mornings. The group plans to rotate volunteers between routes and count at matched times and weather conditions.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which further observation would best support a shrub-related difference?
options: The routes display different sign colours.
The observers visit both routes less often.
The windy route receives a new gravel surface just before every visit.
The count disparity persists at matched times and weather and is concentrated near the shrubs.
questions.explanation: Comparable conditions and a difference near the shrubs offer stronger evidence related to planting.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: There are 10 assignments. Two designated assignments must be consecutive, in either order. If just their leftmost starting slot and their internal order are counted, how many placements are possible?
questions.explanation: The consecutive pair can start in any slot except the last and has two orientations.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person walks 30 m west, then 10 m east and 15 m north. What is the distance from the start?
questions.explanation: The net legs are 4k west and 3k north, so the straight-line distance is the 5k hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In file batch 55, A sits left of B; D immediately follows B; C is first and E is last. What is third in the order?
questions.explanation: After fixing the ends, the three middle positions can only be A, B, D.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In team Eluru, P scored higher than Q and R. Q scored higher than S but lower than R. Who placed second?
questions.explanation: The four place in descending order P, R, Q, S.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Fill the blank in 8, 13, …, 23, 28.
questions.explanation: The arithmetic progression increases by five.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Apply the same rule as the sequence 5, 10, 30, 60, 180 to find the next term.
questions.explanation: The multipliers alternate between 2 and 3. After ×3 comes ×2.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The quantities 9 and 27 are paired. Applying the same ratio to 14 gives what paired number?
questions.explanation: The second quantity in the example is three times the first.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: At Eluru, five counters line up in a fixed list. Counter A must come first and counter E last. How many possible orders of the remaining counters meet the requirement that B is before C?
questions.explanation: Of the 3! orders of the middle counters, exactly half have B before C.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Which of these proposed pairs for block 5 fails the rule that the second letter is two alphabet positions after the first, with wraparound?
questions.explanation: The failing pair moves by three positions. The other three move by two.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A number has 2 as its tens digit and 3 as its units digit. What is the difference between the reversed number and the original?
questions.explanation: Swapping digits changes the number by nine times their difference, which is 1.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 8, 11, 17, 26, 38, …
questions.explanation: Differences are successive multiples of 3. The next difference is 15.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 8, 24, 22, 66, 64, …
questions.explanation: Apply ×3 and −2 alternately. The next operation is ×3.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete 7, 45, 11, 42, 15, 39, …
questions.explanation: Odd positions increase by four, while even positions decrease by three. The next position is odd.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: What pair follows UI, TJ, RL, OO, …? The alphabet wraps around.
questions.explanation: The first letter moves backwards and the second forwards by 1, 2, 3 and then 4 places.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: How is ELURU coded if letters in odd positions advance one place and letters in even positions move back two places, wrapping when necessary?
questions.explanation: Apply the alternating shifts independently to each letter. The transformed letters are F, J, V, P, V.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Encode ELURU by moving every letter back one place and then reversing the result. The letter before A is Z.
questions.explanation: First substitute the preceding letter for each character, then read the substituted word backwards.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person is 15th from the front of a 46-person queue. What is their rank from the back, counting the person?
questions.explanation: Subtract the front rank from the total and add one.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A runner was 13th from the end. After 8 entrants finish behind the runner and two ahead, what is their new rank from the end?
questions.explanation: Only finishers behind the runner increase their rank from the end.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The pair 10 : 120 follows a rule: square the first number and add twice the first number. What pairs with 12?
questions.explanation: Apply n²+2n to 12.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A two-digit number is coded as three times its tens digit plus twice its units digit. What is the code for 29?
questions.explanation: Read the tens and units digits separately and apply the two stated weights.

title: RRB Station Master CBT · Practice model 9
note: A full-length paper with newly parameterised calculations, charts, data sufficiency, comprehension and reasoning. It follows the indicative 30/30/20/20 breakdown.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A lift raises a 55 kg load by 3 m in 6 s at a steady speed. Take g = 10 m/s² and efficiency 75%. What input power is needed to the nearest watt?
questions.explanation: Useful power is (5m)×10×3/6 = 125m watts. Divide by 0.75 to find the input power.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 333 N load acts 20 cm to the left of a frictionless pivot. A 37 N load counterbalances it on the right. What is the right-hand lever arm?
questions.explanation: For equilibrium the moments are equal. The smaller force must have 9 times the lever arm.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Resistors of 8 Ω and 16 Ω are connected in series to 48 V. What power is delivered to the larger resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance is 24 Ω. The series current is 2 A, so the larger resistor receives I²R = 4×16.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two 16 Ω resistors are connected in parallel to 48 V. One branch opens. How much does the current drawn from the source decrease?
questions.explanation: Each connected branch draws V/R = 3 A. Disconnecting one branch removes its 3 A contribution.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 2.5 kW appliance runs for 48 min each day for 10 days. What is its electricity cost at ₹6.50/kWh?
questions.explanation: Forty-eight minutes is 0.8 hour. Multiply power by 8 hours total and then by ₹6.50/kWh.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Mix 600 g of water at 75°C with 1800 g at 15°C in an insulated vessel of negligible heat capacity. What is the equilibrium temperature?
questions.explanation: The cooler water has triple the mass. The weighted mean is (75+3×15)/4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A heater transfers 5400 J of energy into a 0.6 kg metal block. If the temperature rises by 15°C, find the block’s specific heat capacity.
questions.explanation: Use c=Q/(mΔT), which gives 5400 divided by 0.6×15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A linear sensor reads 6 units at 0°C and 112 units at 100°C. What is the reading at 40°C, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: Add 40% of the change from zero to boiling to the sensor’s reading at 0°C.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An ideal pulley system has four rope segments supporting a 360 N load. What is the work done at the free end to raise the load 1.5 m?
questions.explanation: In an ideal machine the input work equals the increase in potential energy: weight × height.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The ordered measurements are 6, 9, 12, 14, 16, 21, 26. The smallest is corrected to 31. What is the new median?
questions.explanation: The corrected value moves to the end. The old fifth observation becomes the new fourth observation.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A workshop pays a fixed fee of ₹91 plus ₹7 per unit. It pays ₹385 total. What would the bill have been if it had used 6 fewer units?
questions.explanation: The fee is unchanged. Subtract 6×₹7 from the original bill.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two adjacent interior angles of a parallelogram differ by 12°. What is the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles sum to 180°. The larger is 90° plus half their stated difference.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A depot marks a spare part at ₹1700. It applies discounts of 20% and then 15%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: Multiply the marked price by 0.8×0.85 = 0.68. The second discount applies to the reduced price.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: After selling 30% of its ticket stock, a depot has 168 tickets. How many would remain if it then sold one-seventh of the remaining tickets?
questions.explanation: The second sale leaves six-sevenths of 168. The original stock is unnecessary for this step.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The mean mass of 22 sacks is 41 kg. Four other sacks averaging 49 kg are added. What is the combined mean to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: Add the two total masses before dividing by the new number of sacks.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: P can complete a task in 36 days and Q in 72 days. They work together for 6 days. How many more days does Q need alone?
questions.explanation: Together they complete k(1/(6k)+1/(12k)) = one-quarter. Q completes the remaining three-quarters in 9k days. Here k = 6.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 216 m train travels at 72 km/h and passes a second train moving towards it at 36 km/h. If the entire pass takes 9 seconds, how long is the second train?
questions.explanation: The combined speed is 30 m/s. Multiply by the passing time to get both lengths together and subtract the length of the first train.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A total of 102 tickets cost ₹3180. Regular tickets cost ₹40 and concession tickets cost ₹25. How many regular tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Subtract what all concession tickets would cost from the actual total, then divide the difference by ₹15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A waiting hall has 20 rows. The first row has 13 seats and each subsequent row has 3 more. How many seats are in the last four rows together?
questions.explanation: The last four rows have L, L−3, L−6 and L−9 seats, where L is the final row count.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A status display refreshes every 24 min and a timer every 36 min. Both refresh at 08:00. How many minutes after 08:00 do they refresh together for the third time, excluding 08:00?
questions.explanation: The joint period is LCM(4k,6k) = 12k, with k = 6. The third joint refresh is after three such periods.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: There are 10 red and 13 blue tokens. Two are sampled without replacement. What is the probability of sampling two reds, to three decimals?
questions.explanation: Multiply the probability of a red first by the conditional probability of another red after one has been removed.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The water level in a cuboid tank of base 30 cm by 24 cm rises from 7 cm to 16 cm when an object is fully submerged. What is the object’s volume?
questions.explanation: The object displaces the base area multiplied by the rise in water level.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A circular island of radius 10 m is surrounded by a walkway 3 m wide. What is the walkway area, in multiples of π?
questions.explanation: Subtract the inner disk from the outer disk: (r+3)²−r² = 6r+9.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 18 m vertical pole casts a 24 m shadow. From the shadow tip what is the cosine of the angle of elevation?
questions.explanation: The right triangle is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle. Cosine is the horizontal side over the hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A metal sheet measures 18 cm by 25 cm and is 4 mm thick. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Convert the thickness to 0.4 cm. Multiplying it by the base area gives 10 times the first side length.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 72 cm³ sample of density 3 g/cm³ is combined with a 48 cm³ sample of density 5 g/cm³ without volume change. What is their combined density?
questions.explanation: The mass is 36k+40k = 76k g and the volume is 20k cm³, where k = 6. Divide to obtain the density.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A component has a mass of 11 kg. What is the decrease in weight when moved from a location with g = 10 m/s² to one with g = 8 m/s²?
questions.explanation: Mass stays constant. Weight changes by the mass times the 2 m/s² difference in g.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 11 kg trolley is pulled east by 77 N and west by 44 N. It starts at rest. How far does it travel in 4 s if the forces are constant?
questions.explanation: The net force is 3 times the mass, giving 3 m/s² east. From rest, distance = ½×3×4².

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A sliding crate is pulled with a horizontal force of 120 N along 10 m. Kinetic friction is 40 N. What is the net work on the crate?
questions.explanation: Only horizontal forces do work here. Their net value is twice the friction force in the direction of travel.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 11 kg object slows from 8 m/s to 4 m/s. Find the magnitude of net work done during braking.
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the kinetic energy decrease is ½m(8²−4²) = 24m.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: What was the combined on-time departure rate, to one decimal place?

questions.question: Counters P and Q sold 172 tickets together. How many did P sell? I. P sold 12 more than Q. II. P sold more than 40 tickets.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A service by Guntakal has a total of 360 seats in two coaches. How many seats does coach A have? I. A has more seats than B. II. B has exactly 130 seats.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A dispatcher at Guntakal sees two queues. Is the service rate of X higher than that of Y? I. X serves three times as many people. II. X takes twice as long for that number. Both counts are positive.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three docks dispatched 36, 46, and 56 parcels in some order. B dispatched more than C. A did not dispatch the fewest or the most. What was B’s count?
questions.explanation: A must be the middle dock. Of the remaining two, B is larger.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three weekly totals average 86. The first two were 71 and 96. What was the final total?
questions.explanation: Multiply the mean by three, then subtract the two known observations.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A review at Guntakal was held on Sunday. What weekday is the next review if it is 72 days later?
questions.explanation: The day shift is the remainder when 72 is divided by seven.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Farah is the sister of Indu. Indu is the mother of Mina. How is Farah related to Mina?
questions.explanation: The person described is the sister of the child’s mother.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What negates the claim “Every consignment checked at Guntakal was both tagged and sealed”?
options: Every checked consignment was untagged and unsealed.
Some checked consignments were both tagged and sealed.
At least one checked consignment was untagged or unsealed.
questions.explanation: To refute the universal claim, one checked consignment need only fail either requirement.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Guntakal, exactly two tasks are selected from A, B, C and D. Choosing A requires C. Tasks B and C cannot both be selected. Which pair is valid?
questions.explanation: The pair includes A’s prerequisite and avoids the prohibited combination.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Some enquiries at Guntakal are forwarded. Every forwarded enquiry receives a tracking number. Some enquiries are urgent. What is certain?
options: Every enquiry with a tracking number is urgent.
No enquiry with a tracking number is urgent.
questions.explanation: At least one forwarded enquiry exists, and every forwarded enquiry receives a number. Urgency is unrelated in the premises.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Only one of Farah, Indu and Mina signed a receipt. Farah says that Indu signed it. Indu says that Mina signed it. Mina says that Indu did not sign it. Exactly two statements are true. Who signed it?
questions.explanation: The statements by the first and third people are complements. The middle statement must be true as well.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A box may leave shelf 46 only when it has passed inspection and has a collection code. A box has passed inspection and lacks a collection code. What follows?
options: It may not leave under this rule.
It necessarily belongs to another shelf.
questions.explanation: Passing inspection meets one requirement. A collection code is also required.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Surveyors at Guntakal interviewed only passengers who arrived before 08:00. Most interviewed passengers favoured a morning service. Which conclusion is defensible?
options: Most passengers at all hours favoured the service.
Most members of the interviewed group favoured the service.
The survey sampled all types of passengers equally.
questions.explanation: The survey supports a statement about its sample. The time restriction limits broader inference.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Guntakal, a form is accepted whenever its two signatures are present. A particular form was not accepted. What must follow?
options: At least one signature was absent.
The form was accepted without a signature.
questions.explanation: If both signatures were present, the rule would guarantee acceptance. Nonacceptance rules out both being present.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: During review 16, case P is earlier than Q. R is earlier than P and S is later than Q. Which case is third in time order?
questions.explanation: The constraints force R, P, Q, S in that order.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Guntakal, all inspected consignments are tagged. No tagged consignment is in bay Z. Some priority consignments are inspected. Which conclusion is forced?
options: Some priority consignments are outside bay Z.
Some inspected consignments are in bay Z.
Every consignment outside bay Z is tagged.
questions.explanation: An inspected priority consignment is tagged and therefore outside bay Z.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An office in Guntakal moves a help desk next to the numbered gates to cut requests for directions. Which assumption is needed?
options: All visitors prefer speaking to an official.
The desk handles refunds at every gate.
The number of gates will decrease.
Some people needing directions can find the relocated desk.
questions.explanation: For the relocation to affect direction requests, at least some intended users must be able to reach the desk.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: After a digital guide was installed at Guntakal, missed connections fell. Which observation most weakens the argument that the guide caused the reduction?
options: The guide uses larger text than the old notice.
The timetable simultaneously lengthened the connection windows.
The total number of express routes remained steady.
Users consulted the guide on both weekdays and weekends.
questions.explanation: More time to connect is an alternative explanation that changed when the guide changed.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Guntakal, two switches start open. An indicator turns on exactly when one switch is closed. The first switch is now closed and the indicator is off. What follows?
questions.explanation: With the first switch closed, an open second switch would turn the indicator on.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: The rule at Guntakal states that each accepted request has a reference number. Request 36 has no reference number. What can be concluded?
options: The request was accepted with a special code.
All requests without account IDs are accepted.
questions.explanation: An accepted request necessarily has a reference number. Its absence rules out acceptance.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 3:11?
questions.explanation: The minute hand is at 66°. The hour hand is at 95.5°. Take the smaller angular separation.

questions.subject: Logical Capability

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In file batch 56, A sits left of B; D immediately follows B; C is first and E is last. What is third in the order?
questions.explanation: After fixing the ends, the three middle positions can only be A, B, D.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In team Guntakal, P scored higher than Q and R. Q scored higher than S but lower than R. Who placed second?
questions.explanation: The four place in descending order P, R, Q, S.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Fill the blank in 9, 14, …, 24, 29.
questions.explanation: The arithmetic progression increases by five.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Apply the same rule as the sequence 6, 12, 36, 72, 216 to find the next term.
questions.explanation: The multipliers alternate between 2 and 3. After ×3 comes ×2.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The quantities 10 and 30 are paired. Applying the same ratio to 15 gives what paired number?
questions.explanation: The second quantity in the example is three times the first.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: At Guntakal, five counters line up in a fixed list. Counter A must come first and counter E last. How many possible orders of the remaining counters meet the requirement that B is before C?
questions.explanation: Of the 3! orders of the middle counters, exactly half have B before C.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Which of these proposed pairs for block 6 fails the rule that the second letter is two alphabet positions after the first, with wraparound?
questions.explanation: The failing pair moves by three positions. The other three move by two.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A number has 2 as its tens digit and 4 as its units digit. What is the difference between the reversed number and the original?
questions.explanation: Swapping digits changes the number by nine times their difference, which is 2.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 9, 13, 21, 33, 49, …
questions.explanation: Differences are successive multiples of 4. The next difference is 20.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 9, 27, 25, 75, 73, …
questions.explanation: Apply ×3 and −2 alternately. The next operation is ×3.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete 8, 46, 12, 43, 16, 40, …
questions.explanation: Odd positions increase by four, while even positions decrease by three. The next position is odd.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: What pair follows VJ, UK, SM, PP, …? The alphabet wraps around.
questions.explanation: The first letter moves backwards and the second forwards by 1, 2, 3 and then 4 places.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: How is GUNTA coded if letters in odd positions advance one place and letters in even positions move back two places, wrapping when necessary?
questions.explanation: Apply the alternating shifts independently to each letter. The transformed letters are H, S, O, R, B.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Encode GUNTA by moving every letter back one place and then reversing the result. The letter before A is Z.
questions.explanation: First substitute the preceding letter for each character, then read the substituted word backwards.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person is 16th from the front of a 48-person queue. What is their rank from the back, counting the person?
questions.explanation: Subtract the front rank from the total and add one.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A runner was 14th from the end. After 9 entrants finish behind the runner and two ahead, what is their new rank from the end?
questions.explanation: Only finishers behind the runner increase their rank from the end.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The pair 11 : 143 follows a rule: square the first number and add twice the first number. What pairs with 13?
questions.explanation: Apply n²+2n to 13.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A two-digit number is coded as three times its tens digit plus twice its units digit. What is the code for 30?
questions.explanation: Read the tens and units digits separately and apply the two stated weights.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: There are 11 assignments. Two designated assignments must be consecutive, in either order. If just their leftmost starting slot and their internal order are counted, how many placements are possible?
questions.explanation: The consecutive pair can start in any slot except the last and has two orientations.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person walks 36 m west, then 12 m east and 18 m north. What is the distance from the start?
questions.explanation: The net legs are 4k west and 3k north, so the straight-line distance is the 5k hypotenuse.

title: RRB Station Master CBT · Practice model 10
note: A full-length paper with newly parameterised calculations, charts, data sufficiency, comprehension and reasoning. It follows the indicative 30/30/20/20 breakdown.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two 18 Ω resistors are connected in parallel to 54 V. One branch opens. How much does the current drawn from the source decrease?
questions.explanation: Each connected branch draws V/R = 3 A. Disconnecting one branch removes its 3 A contribution.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 2.75 kW appliance runs for 48 min each day for 10 days. What is its electricity cost at ₹6.50/kWh?
questions.explanation: Forty-eight minutes is 0.8 hour. Multiply power by 8 hours total and then by ₹6.50/kWh.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Mix 700 g of water at 75°C with 2100 g at 15°C in an insulated vessel of negligible heat capacity. What is the equilibrium temperature?
questions.explanation: The cooler water has triple the mass. The weighted mean is (75+3×15)/4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A heater transfers 6300 J of energy into a 0.7 kg metal block. If the temperature rises by 15°C, find the block’s specific heat capacity.
questions.explanation: Use c=Q/(mΔT), which gives 6300 divided by 0.7×15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A linear sensor reads 7 units at 0°C and 114 units at 100°C. What is the reading at 40°C, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: Add 40% of the change from zero to boiling to the sensor’s reading at 0°C.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An ideal pulley system has four rope segments supporting a 420 N load. What is the work done at the free end to raise the load 1.5 m?
questions.explanation: In an ideal machine the input work equals the increase in potential energy: weight × height.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The ordered measurements are 7, 10, 13, 15, 17, 22, 27. The smallest is corrected to 32. What is the new median?
questions.explanation: The corrected value moves to the end. The old fifth observation becomes the new fourth observation.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A workshop pays a fixed fee of ₹92 plus ₹7 per unit. It pays ₹400 total. What would the bill have been if it had used 6 fewer units?
questions.explanation: The fee is unchanged. Subtract 6×₹7 from the original bill.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two adjacent interior angles of a parallelogram differ by 14°. What is the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles sum to 180°. The larger is 90° plus half their stated difference.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A depot marks a spare part at ₹1800. It applies discounts of 20% and then 15%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: Multiply the marked price by 0.8×0.85 = 0.68. The second discount applies to the reduced price.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: After selling 30% of its ticket stock, a depot has 175 tickets. How many would remain if it then sold one-seventh of the remaining tickets?
questions.explanation: The second sale leaves six-sevenths of 175. The original stock is unnecessary for this step.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The mean mass of 24 sacks is 41 kg. Four other sacks averaging 50 kg are added. What is the combined mean to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: Add the two total masses before dividing by the new number of sacks.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: P can complete a task in 42 days and Q in 84 days. They work together for 7 days. How many more days does Q need alone?
questions.explanation: Together they complete k(1/(6k)+1/(12k)) = one-quarter. Q completes the remaining three-quarters in 9k days. Here k = 7.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 240 m train travels at 72 km/h and passes a second train moving towards it at 36 km/h. If the entire pass takes 10 seconds, how long is the second train?
questions.explanation: The combined speed is 30 m/s. Multiply by the passing time to get both lengths together and subtract the length of the first train.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A total of 114 tickets cost ₹3555. Regular tickets cost ₹40 and concession tickets cost ₹25. How many regular tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Subtract what all concession tickets would cost from the actual total, then divide the difference by ₹15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A waiting hall has 22 rows. The first row has 13 seats and each subsequent row has 3 more. How many seats are in the last four rows together?
questions.explanation: The last four rows have L, L−3, L−6 and L−9 seats, where L is the final row count.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A status display refreshes every 28 min and a timer every 42 min. Both refresh at 08:00. How many minutes after 08:00 do they refresh together for the third time, excluding 08:00?
questions.explanation: The joint period is LCM(4k,6k) = 12k, with k = 7. The third joint refresh is after three such periods.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: There are 11 red and 14 blue tokens. Two are sampled without replacement. What is the probability of sampling two reds, to three decimals?
questions.explanation: Multiply the probability of a red first by the conditional probability of another red after one has been removed.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The water level in a cuboid tank of base 35 cm by 24 cm rises from 7 cm to 17 cm when an object is fully submerged. What is the object’s volume?
questions.explanation: The object displaces the base area multiplied by the rise in water level.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A circular island of radius 11 m is surrounded by a walkway 3 m wide. What is the walkway area, in multiples of π?
questions.explanation: Subtract the inner disk from the outer disk: (r+3)²−r² = 6r+9.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 21 m vertical pole casts a 28 m shadow. From the shadow tip what is the cosine of the angle of elevation?
questions.explanation: The right triangle is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle. Cosine is the horizontal side over the hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A metal sheet measures 19 cm by 25 cm and is 4 mm thick. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Convert the thickness to 0.4 cm. Multiplying it by the base area gives 10 times the first side length.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 84 cm³ sample of density 3 g/cm³ is combined with a 56 cm³ sample of density 5 g/cm³ without volume change. What is their combined density?
questions.explanation: The mass is 36k+40k = 76k g and the volume is 20k cm³, where k = 7. Divide to obtain the density.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A component has a mass of 12 kg. What is the decrease in weight when moved from a location with g = 10 m/s² to one with g = 8 m/s²?
questions.explanation: Mass stays constant. Weight changes by the mass times the 2 m/s² difference in g.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 12 kg trolley is pulled east by 84 N and west by 48 N. It starts at rest. How far does it travel in 4 s if the forces are constant?
questions.explanation: The net force is 3 times the mass, giving 3 m/s² east. From rest, distance = ½×3×4².

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A sliding crate is pulled with a horizontal force of 135 N along 11 m. Kinetic friction is 45 N. What is the net work on the crate?
questions.explanation: Only horizontal forces do work here. Their net value is twice the friction force in the direction of travel.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 12 kg object slows from 8 m/s to 4 m/s. Find the magnitude of net work done during braking.
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the kinetic energy decrease is ½m(8²−4²) = 24m.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A lift raises a 60 kg load by 3 m in 6 s at a steady speed. Take g = 10 m/s² and efficiency 75%. What input power is needed to the nearest watt?
questions.explanation: Useful power is (5m)×10×3/6 = 125m watts. Divide by 0.75 to find the input power.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 380 N load acts 20 cm to the left of a frictionless pivot. A 38 N load counterbalances it on the right. What is the right-hand lever arm?
questions.explanation: For equilibrium the moments are equal. The smaller force must have 10 times the lever arm.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Resistors of 9 Ω and 18 Ω are connected in series to 54 V. What power is delivered to the larger resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance is 27 Ω. The series current is 2 A, so the larger resistor receives I²R = 4×18.

questions.question: Counters P and Q sold 184 tickets together. How many did P sell? I. P sold 14 more than Q. II. P sold more than 40 tickets.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A service by Hindupur has a total of 380 seats in two coaches. How many seats does coach A have? I. A has more seats than B. II. B has exactly 135 seats.
questions.explanation: Subtract the known B count from the total. Knowing only which is larger does not determine the count.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A dispatcher at Hindupur sees two queues. Is the service rate of X higher than that of Y? I. X serves three times as many people. II. X takes twice as long for that number. Both counts are positive.
