questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three docks dispatched 37, 47, and 57 parcels in some order. B dispatched more than C. A did not dispatch the fewest or the most. What was B’s count?
questions.explanation: A must be the middle dock. Of the remaining two, B is larger.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three weekly totals average 87. The first two were 72 and 97. What was the final total?
questions.explanation: Multiply the mean by three, then subtract the two known observations.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Gita is the sister of Jaya. Jaya is the mother of Nila. How is Gita related to Nila?
questions.explanation: The person described is the sister of the child’s mother.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What negates the claim “Every consignment checked at Hindupur was both tagged and sealed”?
options: Every checked consignment was untagged and unsealed.
Some checked consignments were both tagged and sealed.
At least one checked consignment was untagged or unsealed.
questions.explanation: To refute the universal claim, one checked consignment need only fail either requirement.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Hindupur, exactly two tasks are selected from A, B, C and D. Choosing A requires C. Tasks B and C cannot both be selected. Which pair is valid?
questions.explanation: The pair includes A’s prerequisite and avoids the prohibited combination.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Some enquiries at Hindupur are forwarded. Every forwarded enquiry receives a tracking number. Some enquiries are urgent. What is certain?
options: Every enquiry with a tracking number is urgent.
No enquiry with a tracking number is urgent.
questions.explanation: At least one forwarded enquiry exists, and every forwarded enquiry receives a number. Urgency is unrelated in the premises.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Only one of Gita, Jaya and Nila signed a receipt. Gita says that Jaya signed it. Jaya says that Nila signed it. Nila says that Jaya did not sign it. Exactly two statements are true. Who signed it?
questions.explanation: The statements by the first and third people are complements. The middle statement must be true as well.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A box may leave shelf 47 only when it has passed inspection and has a collection code. A box has passed inspection and lacks a collection code. What follows?
options: It may not leave under this rule.
It necessarily belongs to another shelf.
questions.explanation: Passing inspection meets one requirement. A collection code is also required.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Surveyors at Hindupur interviewed only passengers who arrived before 08:00. Most interviewed passengers favoured a morning service. Which conclusion is defensible?
options: Most passengers at all hours favoured the service.
Most members of the interviewed group favoured the service.
The survey sampled all types of passengers equally.
questions.explanation: The survey supports a statement about its sample. The time restriction limits broader inference.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Hindupur, a form is accepted whenever its two signatures are present. A particular form was not accepted. What must follow?
options: At least one signature was absent.
The form was accepted without a signature.
questions.explanation: If both signatures were present, the rule would guarantee acceptance. Nonacceptance rules out both being present.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: During review 17, case P is earlier than Q. R is earlier than P and S is later than Q. Which case is third in time order?
questions.explanation: The constraints force R, P, Q, S in that order.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Hindupur, all inspected consignments are tagged. No tagged consignment is in bay Z. Some priority consignments are inspected. Which conclusion is forced?
options: Some priority consignments are outside bay Z.
Some inspected consignments are in bay Z.
Every consignment outside bay Z is tagged.
questions.explanation: An inspected priority consignment is tagged and therefore outside bay Z.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An office in Hindupur moves a help desk next to the numbered gates to cut requests for directions. Which assumption is needed?
options: All visitors prefer speaking to an official.
The desk handles refunds at every gate.
The number of gates will decrease.
Some people needing directions can find the relocated desk.
questions.explanation: For the relocation to affect direction requests, at least some intended users must be able to reach the desk.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: After a digital guide was installed at Hindupur, missed connections fell. Which observation most weakens the argument that the guide caused the reduction?
options: The guide uses larger text than the old notice.
The timetable simultaneously lengthened the connection windows.
The total number of express routes remained steady.
Users consulted the guide on both weekdays and weekends.
questions.explanation: More time to connect is an alternative explanation that changed when the guide changed.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At Hindupur, two switches start open. An indicator turns on exactly when one switch is closed. The first switch is now closed and the indicator is off. What follows?
questions.explanation: With the first switch closed, an open second switch would turn the indicator on.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: The rule at Hindupur states that each accepted request has a reference number. Request 37 has no reference number. What can be concluded?
options: The request was accepted with a special code.
All requests without account IDs are accepted.
questions.explanation: An accepted request necessarily has a reference number. Its absence rules out acceptance.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 4:12?
questions.explanation: The minute hand is at 72°. The hour hand is at 126°. Take the smaller angular separation.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A review at Hindupur was held on Monday. What weekday is the next review if it is 76 days later?
questions.explanation: The day shift is the remainder when 76 is divided by seven.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Why did the team request equal practice time?
options: Practice time determines how many participants are recruited.
Extra practice is a possible explanation for the earlier improvement.
Worked examples can be used only during testing.
Equal time makes the two groups’ answers identical.
questions.explanation: Holding practice time constant helps isolate the effect of worked examples.
questions.passage: A training team added worked examples before a timed assessment. The next intake answered more questions correctly, but had also received more practice time. The team proposed assigning equal practice time to two comparable groups, with only one group receiving worked examples, and testing both groups on previously unseen questions.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Why use previously unseen assessment questions?
options: They guarantee the assessment is easier than the examples.
They give a better test of whether participants can apply the methods to new items.
They ensure participants spend less time preparing.
They make it impossible to score answers.
questions.explanation: Unseen problems test transfer beyond remembering the examples.
questions.passage: A training team added worked examples before a timed assessment. The next intake answered more questions correctly, but had also received more practice time. The team proposed assigning equal practice time to two comparable groups, with only one group receiving worked examples, and testing both groups on previously unseen questions.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which comparison best fits the proposed design?
options: One group gets additional time and the other gets a different test.
Both groups receive examples with no record of practice time.
Two comparable groups get the same time and assessment, with examples available to one group.
Only the highest-scoring group is assessed.
questions.explanation: The intended design changes only access to examples between groups.
questions.passage: A training team added worked examples before a timed assessment. The next intake answered more questions correctly, but had also received more practice time. The team proposed assigning equal practice time to two comparable groups, with only one group receiving worked examples, and testing both groups on previously unseen questions.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which assertion is unsupported by the initial improvement alone?
options: The worked examples were the sole cause.
The next intake answered more questions correctly.
The next intake received more practice time.
The team proposed a more controlled comparison.
questions.explanation: Both changed practice time and worked examples could contribute to the initial difference.
questions.passage: A training team added worked examples before a timed assessment. The next intake answered more questions correctly, but had also received more practice time. The team proposed assigning equal practice time to two comparable groups, with only one group receiving worked examples, and testing both groups on previously unseen questions.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Fill the blank in 10, 15, …, 25, 30.
questions.explanation: The arithmetic progression increases by five.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Apply the same rule as the sequence 7, 14, 42, 84, 252 to find the next term.
questions.explanation: The multipliers alternate between 2 and 3. After ×3 comes ×2.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The quantities 11 and 33 are paired. Applying the same ratio to 16 gives what paired number?
questions.explanation: The second quantity in the example is three times the first.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: At Hindupur, five counters line up in a fixed list. Counter A must come first and counter E last. How many possible orders of the remaining counters meet the requirement that B is before C?
questions.explanation: Of the 3! orders of the middle counters, exactly half have B before C.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Which of these proposed pairs for block 7 fails the rule that the second letter is two alphabet positions after the first, with wraparound?
questions.explanation: The failing pair moves by three positions. The other three move by two.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A number has 2 as its tens digit and 5 as its units digit. What is the difference between the reversed number and the original?
questions.explanation: Swapping digits changes the number by nine times their difference, which is 3.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 10, 15, 25, 40, 60, …
questions.explanation: Differences are successive multiples of 5. The next difference is 25.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 10, 30, 28, 84, 82, …
questions.explanation: Apply ×3 and −2 alternately. The next operation is ×3.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete 9, 47, 13, 44, 17, 41, …
questions.explanation: Odd positions increase by four, while even positions decrease by three. The next position is odd.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: What pair follows WK, VL, TN, QQ, …? The alphabet wraps around.
questions.explanation: The first letter moves backwards and the second forwards by 1, 2, 3 and then 4 places.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: How is HINDU coded if letters in odd positions advance one place and letters in even positions move back two places, wrapping when necessary?
questions.explanation: Apply the alternating shifts independently to each letter. The transformed letters are I, G, O, B, V.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Encode HINDU by moving every letter back one place and then reversing the result. The letter before A is Z.
questions.explanation: First substitute the preceding letter for each character, then read the substituted word backwards.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person is 17th from the front of a 50-person queue. What is their rank from the back, counting the person?
questions.explanation: Subtract the front rank from the total and add one.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A runner was 15th from the end. After 10 entrants finish behind the runner and two ahead, what is their new rank from the end?
questions.explanation: Only finishers behind the runner increase their rank from the end.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The pair 12 : 168 follows a rule: square the first number and add twice the first number. What pairs with 14?
questions.explanation: Apply n²+2n to 14.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A two-digit number is coded as three times its tens digit plus twice its units digit. What is the code for 31?
questions.explanation: Read the tens and units digits separately and apply the two stated weights.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: There are 12 assignments. Two designated assignments must be consecutive, in either order. If just their leftmost starting slot and their internal order are counted, how many placements are possible?
questions.explanation: The consecutive pair can start in any slot except the last and has two orientations.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person walks 42 m west, then 14 m east and 21 m north. What is the distance from the start?
questions.explanation: The net legs are 4k west and 3k north, so the straight-line distance is the 5k hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In file batch 57, A sits left of B; D immediately follows B; C is first and E is last. What is third in the order?
questions.explanation: After fixing the ends, the three middle positions can only be A, B, D.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In team Hindupur, P scored higher than Q and R. Q scored higher than S but lower than R. Who placed second?
questions.explanation: The four place in descending order P, R, Q, S.

questions.question: The water level in a cuboid tank of base 65 cm by 24 cm rises from 7 cm to 23 cm when an object is fully submerged. What is the object’s volume?

questions.question: A circular island of radius 17 m is surrounded by a walkway 3 m wide. What is the walkway area, in multiples of π?

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A metal sheet measures 25 cm by 25 cm and is 4 mm thick. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Convert the thickness to 0.4 cm. Multiplying it by the base area gives 10 times the first side length.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 156 cm³ sample of density 3 g/cm³ is combined with a 104 cm³ sample of density 5 g/cm³ without volume change. What is their combined density?

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A component has a mass of 18 kg. What is the decrease in weight when moved from a location with g = 10 m/s² to one with g = 8 m/s²?
questions.explanation: Mass stays constant. Weight changes by the mass times the 2 m/s² difference in g.

The survey sampled all types of passengers equally.
